author: operator_1
subject: Water leak SR RF circulator
details: Facilities with security came into the control room asking " Where is the water leak?" . That was the first I new of a water leak. Someone had called security about "Water spraying everywhere is SR 3". Operator A found it spraying at RF area near cav2 where a large line had been capped off in circulator water. Operator A secured that cap but gasket had failed.Facities supervisor and another were cleaning up but system was still pressurized and leaking much slower but still problematic. Shift Lead called Operator B and he is coming in, Operator B had been doing the work earlier. We traced the lines but couldn't find a valve to isolate or where water to pressurize was coming from. That is a closed system but very complicated and intertwined. I checked that the pumps are off.I had walked through the area a couple times earlier and no one was workiing there then but a had noticed that work had been done out there but there was no water leaking about 45 minutes earlier.
category: Operations, RF, Safety, Water and Air

author: operator_4
subject: ID 6-2 bent chamber evaluation
details: Verified that the hard stops are set so that the ID will not touch the chamber.This was done by lowering the ID to 15 mm.  (hard stops are set at 12.54 mm).  Then made a stack of plastic shims (approximately 1.3 mm).  The shim could move easily between the chamber and the magnets. At the center it was somewhat tight on the upper magnets and loose at the lower magnets.  The edges were similar.The same shim would not fit into the hard stop gaps.  So the conclusion is that the hard stop will stop the ID from hitting the chamber.

subject: Troubleshooting SR 12 PST2 "air leak
details: I went out and looked and there is air coming out of many of those PSTs not just PST2. What I saw is consistent with when the air pressure for operating them is lost then restored. They should be cycled down then back up to lock up in correct position. In order to do that we need to remove the PST locks and collars which are controlled as Top-Off aperatures. We will need another operator to verifiy controls in ascc on the Sublimation checklist to remove the locks and collars.For moving them use the PVs SR12C___PSTDWN_BC20 and SR12C___PSTUP__BC22 which I have in Probe/CS-studio on station 7. To lower with SR12C___PSTDWN_BC20 we probably will need to move the SRRF Operate key to Test.

subject: SR 4 contrete door actuation

We found that there was green tape which had been placed on the floor just inside the door apparently for layout and scanning floor. Maintenance Specialist scaped and brushed it off of the drive wheel. We then opened and closed door and cleaned up track areas for all wheels. details: When Leda closed to 5.5 mm, with BRKE 3 traces being out of alignment, most inj shots were below 0.4 mA and we were not able to keep 475 mA. author: operator_1
subject: Followup from yesterday - s05shf2 issue
details: After fixing the FFB 11 issue, we heard from the control room that s05shf2 was not communicating to the control room and the PVs were invalid/white on EDM screens. A technician and I walked out to the power supply in sector 5 and saw LAn error on the front panel. Power cycling the supply and then rebooting the soft IOC genesys fixed the problem. The attached image shows that the power supply had been invalid since Sunday June 30th at ~7:47 PM. Thanks to a team member and a colleague for the help debugging out at the power supply.After the SIOC reboot we noticed that the 4 LN solenoid power supplies reported nominal current readback values but the setpoints were at 0A. With the help of a control room operator after they reach 480mA in the SR, we set the ramp rate to 300 A/sec and then set the setpoint to the golden value. This avoided EPICS ramping the supplies from 0 and the monitor value did not change so that was successful. The control room operator set the ramp rates back to the normal 10A/sec after this and we confirmed all the other TDK power supplies were not impacted by the SIOC reboot.In the manual, the only mention of the "LAn" indicator is during power supply startup: "Switch the power supply AC ON again. See the voltage display shows “LAn” for a few seconds during power-up."

author: operator_2
subject: FFB sector 11 followup
details: Following up from yesterday's FFB issue. Rebooting the CPU card returned networking and EPICS connections to the crate. The RST button is broken so it was difficult to do but with some finagling it worked. Note that the VGA monitor connection does not show any output while in this state, it was not until we rebooted the CPU card that we got feedback on the monitor. The serial port connection also didn't show any prompt. Thanks to a technician and a colleague for the help debugging this.This problem had similar symptons to the earlier DHCP issue but we confirmed there was no network problem. A team member and a colleague let us know that there were no packets coming from the crate on the r87 or r196 ports and no DHCP requests being made. They also tried to turning the network port on/off and arping to it's MAC address to see if that would re-establish some network activity but neither caused any packets to appear. Many thanks to LBL net folks for the quick response and debugging help.Something similar happened to this crate back in May 2023 - https://controls.als.lbl.gov/olog/olog.php?id=157240 It might be worth replcing the CPU card this summer anyways since the RST button is broken and without that working, our only option is to power cycle the crate which will cause the inverpower suppplies to immediatly turn off
category: Accelerator Controls, Beamline Activities, Network Support, Operations

author: operator_3
subject: FFB issue resolved - DHCP
details: The r196 network ACLs were updated on the Monday/Tuesday shutdown and we missed the fact that the r196 needs explicit DHCP access to the r84 network. Oddly, this error didn't impact the controls reboot on Tuesday when we did the operating system reboot for each of the crates. Apparently that doesn't cause a new DHCP lease request to happen.Tonight at around 8:00 the beam was lost and sector 6 fast feedback crate PVs were not visible in the control room. This is likely because the sector 6 crate happened to be the first crate to reach back out to the DHCP server to renew the lease. When it couldn't reach the DHCP server the networking stopped functioning (no EPICS, no ping, etc). During debugging, a colleague and I rebooted crates in sector 4 and sector 5 and found they did not boot at all. This pointed to a network/boot server issue.We reached out to LBL net and a colleague helped us and updated the ACL rules for r196 to add DHCP to r84 (ps2.als.lbl.gov is the DHCP host). Rebooted FFB 4-6 and all came up fine. The colleague suggested we reboot all 12 devices to make sure all work and not rely on the lease renewal. We had the CR power down the supplies and completed the reboot of the crates. Many thanks to a colleague for the help

author: operator_3
subject: Collected HiLo lattice characterization data
details: Following up on the prior shifts, I did one last round to collect characterization data for the HiLo lattice in preparation for the ALS-U RF bellows test after the summer shutdown. The shift had 3 main objectives:1.) Setup and cycle the lattice and see whether injection efficiency still is OK2.) With stored beam, generate closed orbit bumps (x and y) in straights 1 and 2 and save the corrector settings.3.) Record injection trajectories in this lattice.All 3 objectives were achieved, however, with some challenges. The main one was that the BTS B3 power supply is dirfting substantially. So the injection efficieny is constantly evolving and retuning it consistently is hard. A more minor one was that the TxT GUI in Matlab does work to collect data, however, the functions to save trajectories were generating errors that were too complex to troubleshoot on the fly. So the BPM reference trajectory was saved with an older matlab script.

author: operator_1
subject: SR03S-IG1 and BL10.0-IG1
details: There was a discrepancy between front panel reading and EPICS PV  for SR03S___IG1____AM01. EPICS was reading double the presure shown on Ion gauge controller front panel. The EPICS chanel is read via an analogue signal using an IRM.   The backup EPICS channel using GPIB (SR03S___IG1____AM06) showed (as expected) the same value as the front panel.So it looked like a problem reading the value with the IRM, however on investigation with the EMs the analogue output voltage from the gauge controller was the expected value based on the EPICS vacuum reading.The EMs replaced the controller and the front panel reading now matches what is seen by EPICS :)  however the  backup PV, using GPIB is still wrong and is not updating - this is possibly due to the GPIB address on the new controller not being set.  This is not critical and can wait until the long shutdown as this is only a backup PV.Also in vacuumland ...  front end vacuum channel BL100:IG_1:AM00:VAC has been very noisy.  This seems not to be caused by the IRM, as the front panel value is also changing. Investigation by the EMs points to a likely problem at the gauge or cabling. The connector to the controller was warm to the touch, and so the connector was taken apart and inspected (perhaps terminations remade).  It seems to no longer be warm, but the noise is still present.As an interim measure, I have set a software low pass filter in EPICS (SMOO field to 0.9) as an online change (will be lost at reboot), which reduces the noise, until the cause can be identified.

author: operator_2
subject: als-mon Nagios configuration changes
details: The als-mon Nagios server monitors systems within the restricted controls networks.  It was previously on the r71 network, but was molved to the Ctrl/RO-DMZ network during the 6/10-11 maintenance.  That caused many of the PV checks to start failing since als-mon was no longer able to reach the associated IOCs.  In order to reduce false alarms the Nagios email alerts were left disabled during operations.Today the problem was fixed and all PV checks are now working again (some checks are failing due to real issues, not because the PV cannot be reached), and email notifications have been re-enabled.The following changes were needed to fix the problem:1.  Nagios was configured to use the cagw-alsdmz gateway (128.3.92.68).2. The host firewall on als-mon was configured to allow UDP packets from cagw-alsdmz.3.  The cagw-alsdmz gateway address was explicitly set for all IOCs since without that the checks were defaulting to using broadcasts.Alternatively we could have configured Nagios to query the PVs using broadcasts rather than through the gateway.  That would have required configuring the als-mon host firewall to allow connections from all ports >10000 for the broadcast return traffic.  That seemed less secure, plus this way we will know if there is a problem with cagw-alsdmz since all PV checks will start failing.

author: operator_4
subject: 1520: Timing System upgrade
details: The Dual EVG firmware and IOC were upgraded to include the following:1) Added EVG autosave PVsGunBunchToGunBiasGunBunchToInjFieldTriggerTimInjFieldSyncDelaySPTimExtrFieldSyncDelaySPGunBunchDelayGunBunchDelay-1GunBunchDelay-2GunBunchDelay-42) Add BR extraction fine delay funcionalityI added the logic to set B0215:EVR1-Out:UDC0:Delay-SP to 0, 200, 400 or 600 according to the target bucket3 Pvs are implemented on the new Dual EVG IOC: B0215:TimSeqRemainderB0215:TimSeqFineDelayB0215:TimSeqFineDelayOffstThey were removed from the MRF IOC3) Add new end of cycle delay PV:Now, we can extend the end of the sequence by using the PV TimCycleDelay.That PV was removed from the MRF IOC4) Wrong timestamps for devices that use the FPGA timestamp.This was an off by 1 error in which the Dual EVG was sending the currentnumber of seconds to its clients and not the next number of seconds.The way it works, at every PPS the EVG is gonna update it's internal timeOfDaycounter and send the PPS event to the clients. After, the EVG sends 32 "seconds" events.Because of this, the clients were using the previous 32 "seconds" events as the next number of seconds.This fix sends the next number of seconds, which is the expected behavior.

subject: GTB and BTS Tuning Summary
details: After recovering from Mod 1 issues, it took us about two hours to get back to 500 mA with minimal tuning. First, scanned the BR Injection Kicker Delay value to 37220 plus minus 3 and found that 37219 was a good value. Changed IFT from 14210 to 14250, and changed AS2 twice to eliminate the faint streak at the end of the beam at TV3. Also changed MAPH from 0.193 to 0.2725. With LEDA closed, we could be much better, but at least we have a stable beam.

author: operator_3
subject: Modulator 1 Reverse power trip
details: We are experiencing periodic RF reverse trips in Mod1 approximately every 4 to 5 hours. Initially, we reviewed the waveforms on the power meter and found no indication that these signals are real. We inspected the connections from the waveguides (WG) to the LINAC S-Band RF Control Interface chassis, 23W2412, which is responsible for triggering the fault. Upon examining the cables, no correlation was found with the fault.Next, we examined the reverse power signal from the RF distribution chassis at its monitoring point, LINAC RE Monitor, in the 23W2412. The signal did not show any anomalies. We left the oscilloscope connected to gather more data. We now have a strong indication that the issue may be due to drifting, potentially in the set point powered by the +/-15V power supply.The recommendation is to wait 30 minutes, go HV and trigger, and call the RF group for further investigation.

subject: Chain B Shutter Closed BL12.2_PSS111
details: During shift turn over I was informed about BL12.2_PSS111 Safety Shutter Control Chassis has a Chain A and B mismatch for shutters closed. We headed over to the Safety Shutter Control and we found Chain A was ON for shutter closed, however, Chain B was not lit. The hutch is secured. Went to the EPS panel and EPS states 12.2_ PSS111 is in a yellow state(unknown?). We checked the rear of the chassis to verify all connections were correctly secured to the chassis. author: operator_1
subject: Klystron 2 Mod-Anode Cabinet Problems
details: Summary: Klystron 2 Mod-Anode HVPS seems to be having problems with its output. We moved to single mode Klystron 1 for now.Longer version: When the SRRF High Voltage turned off, we noticed that the Klystron site #2 Mod-Anode Cabinet heater did not have any current output, with a Current Control of 40A, with 0A of feedback heater current. I don't remember what the heater voltage was nor got pictures, but remember that it was a non-zero number. We replaced the 30A heater fuse (Bussman AGU-30).While trying to turn it back on, we noticed at this time that Klystron 2 was not reading an appropriate amount of current (.20A when .95A was expected at -36kV). When looking at the Klystron 2 System Control PLC closer, we saw that there was also unexpected readings on the power dissapation (-4.5kV, shouldn't be negative or that low), Mod-Anode Voltage (<1kV, lower that the voltage control), and Mod-Anode current (stuck at -0.1mA). Due to this, we think the Mod-Anode HVPS is a likely possible cause for the trip. See attached pictures for the Klystron 2 System control screen at various voltages.We admin locked the back switch inside the filter cabinet during the transition to single klystron mode.

author: operator_1
subject: BL3.1 filter studies
details:
Yesterday, during AP topoff at 500 mA for checkout of the new timing system, we were able to switch the BL3.1 filter and compare measurement noise vs. gain/exposure.Baseline: previous (thick) filter, 10 Hz update rate, 95 ms shutter time, gain 33. This results in roughly 550 units for the amplitude in both planes. Using our usual averaging for 10 sec duration with sampling every 0.1 sec, we record for rms beam sizes in microns a H/V mean of 42.60/43.29 and a std of 0.231/0.320. This is the situation we are used to seeing during users, about 43 microns vertical beam size with 0.3 microns rms (~0.7% measurement noise). To make sure we are not being fooled by CA/EPICS-MATLAB interplay, we also recorded these values with 0.2-sec sampling for the duration of 20 sec: mean then recorded as 42.480/43.125 with a std of 0.204/0.285.
Changchun then switched us over to the new (thinner) filter. In order to restore to the previous ~550 units amplitude, we adjusted the shutter time down to 45 ms and the gain was backed off from its rail at 33 to 14. The difference was immediately visible (see attached striptool): absolute beam sizes and beam aspect ratio changed, but measurement noise went down considerably. For 10 sec / 0.1 sec we recorded a mean of 51.485/47.334 with a std of 0.062/0.101 (0.2% V noise) and for 20 sec / 0.2 sec the mean was 51.537/47.230 with std 0.064/0.096 (0.2% V noise). So the noise in the V dropped by almost a factor 4 which was immediately visible just looking at the strip chart.
We continued to evaluate what is driving the noise.
- Running at gain 33 but lowering the sampling time to 5.5 ms gives roughly the same amplitude again. For 10 sec / 0.1 sec we recorded a mean of 50.174/46.265 with a std of 0.198/0.286 (0.6% V noise) and for 20 sec / 0.2 sec the mean was 50.167/46.289 with std 0.206/0.371 (0.8% V noise).
- Running then at gain 8 but returning to 95 ms sampling gives roughly the same amplitude again. For 10 sec / 0.1 sec we recorded a mean of 51.640/47.388 with a std of 0.058/0.064 (0.1% V noise) and for 20 sec / 0.2 sec the mean was 51.630/47.406 with std 0.067/0.084 (0.2% V noise).
- Running at gain 8 but lowering sampling to 45 ms sampling gives roughly half the amplitude, as expected. For 10 sec / 0.1 sec we recorded a mean of 51.586/47.410 with a std of 0.073/0.098 (0.2% V noise) and for 20 sec / 0.2 sec the mean was 51.586/47.431 with std 0.073/0.082 (0.2% V noise).
- Running at lowered gain of 4 but returning sampling to 95 ms gives roughly 350 units of amplitude and still a good fit. For 10 sec / 0.1 sec we recorded a mean of 51.782/47.561 with a std of 0.087/0.090 (0.2% V noise) and for 20 sec / 0.2 sec the mean was 51.798/47.517 with std 0.046/0.070 (0.1% V noise). So in spite of lower amplitude, we see very low V noise (almost a factor 5 compared to present) while still remaining compatible with 10 Hz data acquisition rate.
Lowering gain clearly allows for lower measurement noise. So we will have to discuss how to properly calibrate the beamline for the new thinner filter. For now, we migrated back to the previous (thick) filter with the usual BL3.1 settings (95 ms shutter, 33 gain, 10 Hz).

author: operator_2
subject: Issue with Effciency Number in MiniDCCT
details: I was told that BR KE was worked on during the start-up shift and BR Ex Kicker delay number might need adjustments. During tuning, I found that we were missing some single bunch shots (for a reasonable BR beam). So, I started adjusting the delay value. I tried the rage 25854-25847 (in 2 setps changes) and interesting thing happened - at lower number 25849 -25847, the efficiency number blew up. We saw 70% numbers with 25849 but the shots were not strong for a given BR beam, for example, we saw only ~0.9mA shots for ~2nC BR beam when it should be well above 1mA even with 50% efficiency). We got completely ridiculous numbers like 200-300% at 25847.  This effect is repeatble -  the efficiency number goes back to normal range when I changed the kicker delay value back to above 25849. This was observed by all during physic shift yesterday. Note: Leda was at 28 mm.This morning,  Leda is at 5.5 mm. I saw 30%-40% range efficiency in miniDCCT and BR E Kicker dealy was 25849. But the injetion shots were very weak. The single bunch shots were also very poor compared to the BR ICT. I changed the delay to 25847, the efficiency blew up to 50%-70% range. The injection shots were indeed better than before (no more missed SB shots) but not as good as they would be at above 50% efficiecy. So, do not trust the high efficiecy numbers in miniDCCT for now. Look at the delta SR for tuning, as someone pointed out, in Injection Charge Monitor, which reads 30% range now (earlier it read 20% range with 25849).

author: operator_2
subject: Injector tuning/status with the new timinng system
details: After we switched to the new timing system, we needed to change LN MAPH substantially to establish a strong enough beam in the Linac. We went to LN MAPH~7 (new timing system) from ~1.5 (old timing system) which is a very good thing because Linac beam is much more stronger (somewhat more stable) and we have more tuning range (although we had been using MAPH values in the range ~4-8 for as far as I can remember, we had to use low PH setpoint like 2.3-1.2 decreasingly, probably since two/three start-ups ago and we were reaching the limit which is zero. Still, the beam in the Linac was somewhat weak). With this change in PH setpoint, we saw above 2.2nC, for multibunch, and 0.6nC, for single bunch, BR beam a few times yesterday (we only saw this for single bunch, brifely after a signal filter replacement last year, on the egun/linac electronics?).

author: operator_4
subject: Topoff Danfysik Interlock
details: Quick Version: BR Bend's Danfysik Chain B's fan was stalled, causing the chassis to heat up and break the interlock.Long Version: We arrived at the Booster Bend and saw the "Topoff Danfysik Interlock (Intlk)" fault light on on the BR bend. Originally, the Danfysiks located on the Booster topoff box both showed OK by the time we got there. While talking with a colleague about what might be the issue, we noticed a relay that was on before was now off and the Chain B Danfysik's Normal Operation light was off. With these symptoms, the colleague thought the problem would either be with the danfysik's current transducer, the power supply, or that the chassis was getting too hot. We then saw that it's fan was not moving. After the RSSWA was in place, we replaced the faulty fan and reinstalled it. The chassis came back on and if nothing similar happens, then that should be the fix.
category: Electronics Maintenance, Operations, Power Supplies, Safety Interlocks

author: operator_1
subject: Tuning Summary During Fill
details: After turning things back on, beam looked very ugly on LTB TV3 and all through the BTS. Lowered QD Gain substantially, set EG Bias back to 30, cleaned up Mast and AS2 phases, raised BR KI from ~96.5 to 98.6. This resulted in stronger and more consistent booster beam. Turning on BTS trajectory feedback cleaned up the BTS very nicely. We're now seeing >50% efficiency and some shots over 1mA (with LEDA open). Next step is to work on poor single bunch shots.

author: operator_3
subject: Synchrotron Tune Measurement
details: I'm still interested in using a BxB FB system to acquire Qs parasitically at all times, even during users. So for this purpose I'm interested in employing modal analysis with ideally as little excitation as necessary on a minimum number of bunches. During my most recent attempts, I was able to get a clear reading of Qs at 0.00378 (5.76 kHz) during 500 mA topoff using mode 47 (71.6 MHz). I tried to replicate those results and then planned to see if I could apply the long. drive to only few bunches (or just one) with low amplitude and still get just barely enough SNR in modal analysis. However, I had trouble confirming the drive was properly engaged and ran out of time. Will return to this next AP opportunity.

author: operator_1
subject: Revised Topoff Code
details: SB inj has lately been a bit inconsistent so at times this has led to a situation where there were very few equalizer shots due to all SB shots going to cam. This tended to result in a fill pattern where the MB train showed an ratty head.The quality of the MB train tail had been substantially improved by switching to a new topoff fill pattern back in Nov 2023. So I now applied that same idea to the trailing end of the fill pattern in order to get a more homogenous MB train head. Station 1 is running this revised topoff code uncompiled in a MATLAB console. If there are any issues with the new fill at all, this instance can just be force quit and the previous version loaded by launching the usual compiled topoff code.If we confirm throughout the next user run that all is well, I'll compile the new revised topoff code. I've also changed our default cleaning pattern accordingly (315 –> 328) in hwinit. When I compile the changes in topoff, I'll also recompile hwinit and srcontrol. For now the cleaning pattern has been changed by hand. If hwinit needs to be run again, it will revert. Running fixCleaner.m in any MATLAB console initialized to SR should take care of that.

subject: Machine Setup
details: Opened gaps and scraped down to 56 mA. Corrected orbit to 16/17 microns rms. BPMs to low current mode. Measured ORM. details: We turned off the SR Gradient power supply inspected the heat strips on the SCRs and checked the fuses of one that showed elevated temps relative to the others. subject: 1450: LIE08 Troubleshooting
details: LIE08 Crash-off box was troubleshot in the Linac crossconnects in rack LI24. The relay contacts were verified open when the crossconnects to the key switch was disconnected:LI2451 RE1-1: LI2451X-3A to LI2451X-1ALI2451 RE1-2: LI2451X-6A to LI2451X-4ALI2453 RE3-1: LI2453X-23A to LI2453X-21ALI2453 RE3-2: LI2453X-26A to LI2453X-24AWhen checking the crossconnects across the key switch, originally there was no continuity across LI2450X-12A to LI2450X-13A even with the key in and turned. LIE08 PG1 pin M was found loose and was fixed by the EIs.The continuity check for the crossconnects across the key switch was ranging from 2-4 ohms without the key and 0.1 with the key switched. This means the key switch was functionally in a closed position at all times.EMs and EIs opened LIE08 and checked the continuity of the key switch directly with the same results.We sprayed contact cleaner solution on the key switch contacts and turned the key several times to make sure the solution made its way in.The continuity check for the key switch now shows open for no key turned and closed with key turned.The crossconnects LI2450X-12A and LI2450X-16A were reconnected and the rack locked.

author: operator_3
subject: Dumped due to heating & refilled
details: After had Angel had checked out SRRF and could not find anything fundamentally wrong (cav1 tuner loop closed light is broken, not off), we kep seeing losses of chunks of bema along with significant heating of flexbands in the SR02S. Once the d/s spool had gone past 80C I advised ops that we shoulkd dump the beam. They closed shutters, opened gaps, and dumped. After resetting rad monitors, I ran hwinit and loaded a fresh lattice. I cycled our 3HC loops a couple times. Confirmed all SR magnets showed within tolerance. Had ops inject 10 mA. VVM reading and master ph Sp looked fine. LFB/TFB reads and spectra all exactly as expected. Had ops inject to 60 mA and performed OCO. At 60 mA I corrected tunes and measured chromaticity. It is spot on (attached) so most likely all sexrtupoles good.Turned on all FBs and had ops inject to 210 mA. 3HC loops closed at 160 mA as usual, all pwr readings exactly where we want them. Traces look fine. At 210 mA confirmed that ph master SP was being adjusted to minimize servo loop delta. Transition at 200 mA from VVM to loop delta was smooth and uneventful. Had ops inject all the way to 500 mA with equalizer and cam, and then take it into topoff. Closed first 5W, verified all pwr readings normal and optics still properly corrected. Phases unpoerturbed and spot on. Closed all other gaps to user settings. Asked ops to open shutters.SR02 flexband temps have come down considerably, but they are not 100% in equilibrium yet (attached). SR07 chicane flexband is still on its way up but it usually runs around 100C (up to 112 today though). I see no elevated temps anywhere else. I do not see any arc IG2s or straight IGs showing elevated pressures (attached) but we can see that chunks of beam loss this afternoon led to small spikes on SR04S-IG2 (and to lesser degree on IG1). I also note that LFB and TFB have not seen any saturation counts during the entire day since ~10am (when I reset counters), which indicates, in spite of all the problems and chunks of beam lost, we have not gone multibunch unstable as one might expect if we had been ionizing gas somewhere. The fill pattern has lost its low-freq modulation and consequently the phase transient has linearized considerably, however, overall magnitude remains about 20deg, not far below what we observed earlier today, and indeed close to where it usually ends up during users.This remains a bit of mystery. I can only advise to continue to keep a good eye on bellows TCs and pressures. SR02 deserves very close attention.

author: operator_1
subject: SRRF cavity 1 detuned?
details: So with all these recent losses of chunks of stored beam I had inspected 3HC pwr levels. But power levels in all three cavities there look normal (see attached). I then noticed that there was a lot of reverse pwr from main RF cav 1 (also attached). We also see a large phase transient (attached) along with our elevated flexband temps as well as a low lifetime.We were wondering if this large reverse pwr from cav 1 could indicate a relative detuning between the two cavities — this would lower the effective accelerating voltage the beam sees, which could explain the hot flexbands and poor lifetime (via not properly stretched bunches along the train).  took a walk down to the racks and came back with an interesting find on cav 1 tuner (photos attached). The tuner chassis shows loop NOT closed (not open either though). The tuner 1 temp reading is fluctuating a lot showing temps in excess of 100C. Meanwhile the cav 2 tuner is showing loop closed and 36.2C. We did not dare to just push the close loop button in the middle of use rops without consulting with an SRRF expert first. Could an SRRF expert check that cav 1 tuner is in proper working order ASAP?Workarounds would be to detune the 3HCs in an effort to get better bunch legnthening along the entire train (via tuner error setting) or to drop the topoff goal current. Also, on the next beam dump we could recheck the chromaticity (sextupoles affected by recent power outage?) although in light of the elevated reverse pwr, I doubt that the chromaticity is our culprit — it was confirmed fine during the recent setup.

author: operator_3
subject: Beam loss recovery update
details: Following the reset of the house nitrogen system in a previous entry, nitrogen was flowing again.By around 2100, we got the SR RF running. At Du's instruction, disconnecting and reconnecting the fiber optic cable in the port labeled "Fast RF Interlock" on the back of the RF Drive PLC chassis caused the Fast RF permit to make up. We had also discovered an issue where one of the KI power supplies was not going into HV mode, EMs resolved this. When we tried to fill, we were unable to establish beam in the booster, and I discovered it was because Booster QF had not actually ramped up, although BR Control was showing it as being at setpoint and the BR Power Supplies application was not showing the PS faulted.Rebooted dpsc IOC, then saw a Booster QF trace on ramping waveforms application, which was better than we had before. Ramping the BR power supplies normally did not result in them going to setpoint, so ramped each BR large power supply manually to their last saved value.By about 2240, got beam through the booster and BTS with minimal tuning, and began putting beam in the SR, but then began having major complaints from Alarm Handler about the tunes and the TFB, which we have been struggling with since. After injecting for a while, tunes sometimes appear to be improving, and then something seems to push the tunes out of range until eventually the TFB scoops a bunch of beam out, and this has happened several times. We see major instability in TFB application, especially in the vertical. Checked TFB amps and both appear to be running normally. Tried hardware init, tried reselecting User Beam from BPM Control app, tried dumping beam and restarting tunes application and SR control and refilling from 0 mA, nothing seems to be successful.

author: operator_4
subject: ID scanning for ML training data collection
details: Started acquiring training data for ML. In case of beam dump, below are the instructions for recovery. At 7am please stop both scripts, open all ID gaps, dump, and cycle the lattice. Then inject from scratch for users. Please use 500 mA again for the topoff goal until further notice.Instructions to Ops:For the training data acquisition, the machine needs to be in user ops conditions with 500mA top off, all feedbacks and ID FF running (but keep ML ID Feedforward unchecked). BL3.1 image acquisition must be running and ROI FB on as well. ROI FB is running in a window on the right screen of apps1 (which results in the beam being in the center of the BL3.1 screen). In case it’s not running properly you can nuke it and restart it from the ALS launcher under cameras. On appsdev a Matlab instance is open with the script physbase/users/thellert/beamsize/ID_scan/main_240519.mRun the script, for example by pressing the green ‚Run‘ button in the matlab menu or by running the script from the matlab command window. If the script needs to be stopped you can pause and resume it, or start over by aborting the script and run it again.In another idle matlab instance on station 7, run ID_AMP_watchdog.m (om the SR path) since that station produces good sound. subject: BL3.1 filter left unchanged
details: Changchun and I tried to go to the new thinner filter at BL3.1 and convince ourselves that we could update the calibration. We again discovered that, in spite of the beam spot now hitting the thinner filter more centered, the aspect ratio is different between the current thick and the new thinner filter. We were able to verify that bumping the beam locally around the 3.1 source point introduces enough local coupling that the aspect ratio of the beam spot changes, regardless of filter choice. author: operator_4
subject: SRRF Cavity Phase Tuner Problem
details: When we initiated the startup sequence on the SRRF, we encountered issues with both cavities showing low power in the cavity cell and high reverse power. The 500MHz Cavity Phase Tuner Servo Controller Chassis (23W0604) indicated that the cavity's phase was not in the correct position.The reason the chassis calibration was inadequate could be due to the chassis being powered down during the IRM Relocation project. When they were powered back on, they were not in close-loop mode and were operated once in open-loop mode.On the night of May 14th, EM and I attempted to recalibrate the chassis for Cavity 1 in open-loop mode to achieve the lowest reverse power. We encountered issues on the EPICS side that prevented us from manually controlling the cavities. We contacted Tynan, who assisted us in reconfiguring EPICS to allow manual mode control. We then calibrated and closed the loop to maintain cavity phase control in close-loop mode in the SRRF for Cavity 1. Finally, we verified that the signals and power levels were correct.However, we were unsuccessful in performing this process for Cavity 2. The tuner position did not move when we attempted the sequence in open-loop mode. At that point, we began inspecting the mechanical system, including the motor, bellows, and screw, but found nothing abnormal. Additionally, we verified that the potentiometer measuring the tuner position was functioning correctly. We then checked if the issue was with the 500MHz Cavity Phase Tuner Servo Controller Chassis and swapped the chassis with a spare. However, the spare chassis did not function correctly either. We decided to continue troubleshooting in the morning.On May 15th, Ken Baptiste and additional EM personnel arrived to assist with the issue. We opened the chassis and began verifying the signals. During this process, while measuring the output of the first stage of the circuit controlling the tuner position loop (i.e., the motor) in open-loop mode, some components appeared damaged and needed to be replaced. The components included R7, R6, R5, Q1, and Q2. After these repairs, we measured the voltage at this stage, and the knob that moves the motor (tuner position) showed expected readings, allowing us to move the motor and verify the tuner position meter.However, when we disconnected the multimeter, the same problem reoccurred with no motor movement. After checking the grounding, we regained control of the motor.The knob controlling the tuner position was very sensitive, causing large jumps when attempting fine control within a few degrees.After resolving this, we calibrated the phase for both cavities at 10KW. This process involved starting in open-loop mode to find the minimum reverse power using the tuner position knob, then adjusting the phase error meter to 0 degrees with the phase shifter/cable, and finally closing the loop.At this point, we switched the configuration to Auto Ramp and verified that the cavity cells were at 45KW with low reverse power.Lead: A Jurado, K BaptisteEM: P Ramos, E Kawakami, E Andrade, D Fowler, T Ford
category: Electronics Maintenance, Operations, RF, RF Maintenance

author: operator_1
subject: BRRF Cavity Cell Phase Issue
details: When we initiated the startup sequence on the BRRF, we encountered issues with no power in the cavity cell and high reverse power. The 500MHz Cavity Phase Tuner Servo Controller Chassis (23W0604) indicated that the cavity's phase was not in the correct position.The chassis calibration might have been adequate because, during the shutdown, the Twinax connector for the inhibit signal was replaced both in the cable and the chassis. This indicates that the chassis was disconnected and removed. The RF cables at the rear were not removed from the chassis connector but rather from the extensions/phase adjusters coupled to the chassis. After this, the chassis was reconnected.On the night of May 14th, EM and I recalibrated the chassis by disconnecting the Twinax connector for the inhibit signal. In open loop mode, we managed to achieve the lowest reverse power with considerable difficulty. We then closed the loop to control the cavity phase in close-loop mode in the Booster. We reconnected the Twinax connector and returned control to the operators. We verified that the signals and power levels were correct.On May 15th, the tuner's position began to drift upwards, affecting the match of the cavity phase. The operators started increasing the input gain to achieve the desired output gain, which caused a total mismatch.Today, I arrived and noticed that the cavity cell was out of phase. I recalibrated the cavity phase again. This time, I observed on the oscilloscope that the power in the cavity cell was completely unstable, and we lost the match again. After resuming local control, it was nearly impossible to calibrate the cavity phase with the chassis control in open loop. We experienced large jumps in phase error with minor adjustments to the knob and also if you touched the chassis.After consulting with a colleague, we reviewed all the external RF connections and found a faulty RF cable that we used to mechanically adjust the phase in the line monitoring the RF power of the Cavity Cell. We replaced the cable with a similar one to maintain the same phase delay and minimize the impact on the calibration of the Cavity Phase Tuner Servo Controller Chassis.We restarted the cavity phase calibration process, and this time the phase error was more stable. After completing the calibration, we observed that the signals visualized on the oscilloscope from the cavity cell were more stable. A photo of the connector is attached.
category: Electronics Maintenance, Operations, RF, RF Maintenance

author: operator_3
subject: Test the correction scheme of the residual kick from the BTA switcher bend
details: The ALS-U switcher bend B4 could have a 0.4 mrad residual kick on the BTS beam during the accumulator ring commissioning when ALS is in the operation. To simulate this residual kick, the BTS bending magnent B3 (right before the BTA switcher bend) is increased by 0.4 mrad. After this adjustment, it was observed that the injection effciency was down to a few  or zero percent from their norminal value of 30%.To compenstate for this, a local angle bump around B3 was created by powering up the horizontal correctors HCM4 and HCM7. Dialing the simulated corrector strength of HCM4 and HCM7, the injection efficiency was immediately recovered to the norminal 30% or even better.  This angle bump also generated orbit offsets by about 1.0 mm measured by the BPM3 and BPM4 inside the bump, which is also consistent with the simulation. Although the BTS is in a poor operation condition today, the injection efficiency is lower and the shot-to-shot orbit varation is higher (about a few mm), the correction test  is sucessfull and the results confirm the simulation.

author: operator_2
subject: BL3.1 filter realignment
details: In anticipation of our planned filter change at BL3.1, a team member today realigned for us the tank holding the filter. There was a radial shift by +2 mm outboard (corresponding to the 0.5 mm shift at the source point we had determined on AP). Once this realignment had been completed, we opened the photon stop again and saw the beam return well centered in the previous ROI. There was a slight change in signal amplitude in both planes corresponding to a change in filter position hit by beam. I therefore modified our standard BL3.1 gain from 32->33 where we will remain until we can switch to the new filter setup at the next AP opportunity.For the duration of this realignment and reocnfiguration (and including the PQube beam trip) I had inhibted the ML-based ID FF (since its online fine-tuning relies on the BL3.1 camera image and introduces a FB component) and turned off online fine-tuning. After the BL3.1 image had been restored, I flushed buffers and turned the ML FF back on. All good.

author: operator_3
subject: SEN feedback
details: While we've switched to a new PS for the SR SEK, the SEN remains as it was. Lately, it's been observed that, depending on SEK setpoint, operators needed to tweak the SEN every so often to get optimal capture in the SR. I've therefore put together a simple feedback with some adaptive gain control to adjust the SEN in small increments in order to optimize BTS-SR capture efficiency.This FB is running on apps3 in a MATLAB console at the very SW corner of the screens. I've instructed ops to feel free to turn it off (ctrl-c) if they fear it's interfering with injection. Just like the SEK feedback before, this SEN feedback does not fight manual adjustemnt or operator tuning. The SEN can be tuned by hand while the SEN feedback is running. The FB will respect whatever the most recent manual input was and tune from there. Unlike the BTS traj FB, there should be no attempt of this FB to fight manual input or tuning.After running it for a couple hours I see no major drift. It has tuned within a very tight band so far (within roughly ±3 units on 1760). The FB itself can be found on the main SR path under senFB.m.

subject: Multiple ID's in whiteout on control panel
details: 5 ID’s on the control panel were in whiteout mode.  (8,9,10,12, 6-2).  All these ID’s are on the same ppmac (ppmac01).  Rebooting the ppmac fixed the problem.Below is a detailed description of the process of finding and fixing.The control room thought operator_1 might be rebooting the ppmac and called for info. I logged into the ppmac and observed that srioc12u ioc was spinning and using all the processor power, thus preventing any pv updates from all the devices on the ppmac.  (used the top command).  I then logged into the IDE an tried basic communication with ID12.  I tried to read the station number from the terminal using the commandms24,i11.  The response was a timeout.  ms24,i11stdin:6:1: error #50: MACRO COM TIMEOUT: ms24,i11The actual response should bems24,i11$00000000001cThere had been an incident 10 minutes earlier where the control room was lowering 6-2 to small gap.  During this process three of the ID’s had a fatal following error while sitting still (6-2, 9, 12).  I re-enabled the amplifiers for those ID’s, but only moved ID 6-2.  This may have been caused by an error in the macro ring. Attempting to home a system in this state will cause the ioc to spin.  But I am not sure what actually happened to cause the loss of communication on the macro ring to ID 12.

author: operator_3
subject: HiLo (horizontal beta function) lattice cleanup
details: Resumed cleanup of the HiLo lattice - in preparation for ALS-U RF bellows test at end of summer shutdown. Had substantially more success than the last time and also understood, why orbit correction last time did not work.Started as previously: Switched to 1.9 GeV Top-Off mode in middle layer - this is where the lattice is saved.Cycled lattice using srramp: srramp(1.522,'LinearByEnergy') and srramp(1.89,'LinearByEnergy') - Superbends are slowing down rampLoaded production lattice of Top-Off mode - this is the HiLo latticeAt first did not have any injection, raising nu_x by 0.04 solved that problem. Was able to fill to 10 mA. I had made the orbit repsone matrix from the shift in April the default and orbit correction with it worked fine. Afterwards injection efficiency was up to 1 mA/shot.However, tune measurements were inconclusive, nu_y seemed to be close to an integer (periodicity of 18 turns in turn by turn data). Measured response matrix, LOCO fit did not converge and vertical response was very large - consistent with being very close to the integer resonance.Empirically checked and found that the tune wwas actually just below 9 (around 8.95 instead of the desired 9.20). This explained the orbit response, failure of LOCO convergence and also why in the last shift orbit correction with more nominal repsonse martix data had not worked. So, I deced to get closer to the desired lattice and moved the vertical tune up by 0.25. This of course killed the beam but afterwards injection was again reasonable, albeit with slightly lower efficiency.Filled to 35 mA, corrected orbit, tune, added -1 mm injection straight DC bump and measured another LOCO data set. This time it did converge, showed reasonable agreement with nominal tunes and reasonable agreement with desired beta functions (the lattice has the 33 m, 7 m nominal beta_x in the high / low beta straights, however it is not totally symmetric in y, either - fit looked close enough to desired results).Saved golden lattice, response matrix, ... Tested injecting to 100 and 200 mA. Works fine. Beam interestingly stays stable when one turns the TFBs off. It was not needed to retune them to the different tunes. Injection efficiency is reasonable in this lattice, but not as great with the nominal tunes as in cases where one is somewhat further away from them. This also is related with dose rates in the radiation area on the roof elevated, but it seemd still OK for the fill to 200 mA.Overall this seems like a very good starting point for the test after the summer shutdown. The lattice is clean. We can reach at least 200 mA stable beam, the beta function ratio of 33 / 7 m is much larger than what we had the last time (24 / 8 m), which should keep the injection rate with the rf bellows higher. Only thing I still need to complete in a later shift is to repeat this (to see, that it is reproducible after a few weeks) and to record reference injection trajectories, so that we can correct to them, if unexpected problems occurr during the test,

author: operator_4
subject: BRRF Cavity Power
details: The Booster RF power (can be seen on HPA screen) dropped to low, unusable level (see before picture). The Cavity Power was low (can see from Cav Cell readout and oscilloscope), Waveguide reverse power was high (can also be seen with the power monitor and BR4_____WGREC__AM01), and the phase error on 10° scale would hang around 0° and would budge a little bit positive during a pulse.After discussion with a colleague, I jiggled the Trigger Inhibit cable/connectior and the problem corrected itself. Do note that it took a couple of tries.Included is a video of more normal operation of a couple of the 500M tuner chassis and the power values

I've only briefly tested it and observed that it caught the condition (on a SB shot) and also that it didn't appear to screw up injection or the BTS BPM readings. This was only a very brief test so I left it on for more observation and instructed operators to just ctrl-c it if they at any time believe it is rendering bad injection or interfering with their injection tuning.

subject: LEDA optics perturbations

author: operator_3
subject: Machine setup
details: Loaded lattice, injected to 60 mA, and corrected orbit to 17/19 microns rms. BPMs to low current mode. Measured ORM. LOCO converged after 3 iterations to 2.780 microns rms of measured (1 outlier) with chi^2/DOF = 20.778. ±4% beta beat.Symmetrized and corrected coupling. BPMs back to user mode. OCO to 17/19 microns rms of golden and tunes at 0.158/0.251. Checked all CMs good. Saved golden.Cycled. Injected to 60 mA. OCO to 17/19 microns rms of golden. Corrected tunes 0.1509/0.2464 –> 0.160/0.250. Saved new golden lattice.Injected to 500 mA with all FBs. At 500 mA in topoff measured BL31 beam sizes 45.9/47.6 microns rms. Corrected (-0.0459 on skew wave) to 45.8 microns rms. Lifetime is 5.9 hrs, SR capture is 45%. Saved new golden skews (to MML, feedback script, and new skew IOC). Closed 5W and measured 45.7/46.5 microns rms with lifetime 5.4 hrs. SR capture efficiency is 44%. Verified BSC recorded offsets. Adjusted its target V beam size to 43.7 microns. Closed all IDs to user gaps. Measured 45.4/43.6 microns rms and 4.5 hrs lifetime. SR capture eff now at 27%. Measured chroma with only 5W closed as 1.25/1.52. All done.

author: operator_3
subject: Verification JH scraper settings
details: With 500 mA topoff, user gaps, and LEDA at 5.5 mm I see 0.85 mr/h on average for the monitor at the GEMINI carbon filter.By closing the JH scrapers some more we should be able, according to prior studies with Stefania (Feb 2023), to lower GEMINI dose at the expense of lifetime and perhaps injection efficiency. Since lifetime presently leaves some margin, we could attempt to lower the JH scrapers corresponding to another 5% in lifetime and see how much this lowers dose as well as, and perhaps more importantly, if we still have sufficient inj efficiency.For this purpose I recalibrated the JH scrapers and calculated potential new settings. The shift of goldens is relatively small and as usual due to non-negligible error from lifetime noise in 16b mode as well as exact choice of fit parameters/ranges.The following has been recorded in the order old golden, new golden, tighter setting:JH 1,4t: 0.585, 0.530, 0.444JH 1,4b: 0.303, 0.102, 0.015JH 1,1t: 1.354, 1.708, 1.353JH 1,1b: 2.357, 2.449, 2.118Only JH 1,4b shows a more significant deviation from the recent calibration. And this scraper has always been the hardest to calibrate due to limited travel and its required proximity to beam.For now I am leaving the scraper goldens where they were last set. We can switch to the tighter new values at an upcoming physics when there is time to study the impact on rad/lifetime/inj.

author: operator_4
subject: Lost BRRF pwr to cavity
details: In the middle of calibrating JH scrapers when I asked ops to refill, we noticed that BRRF pwr to cavity had dropped off to ~9 kW in spite of unchanged gain. Both the ZTEC and HSD waveforms showed the same lack of cav pwr. We went back to low gain ansd tried ramping up by hand to no avail. We shut it off, went through the whole sequence to turned it back on, and ramped gain up slowly, but again no improvement. We asked EMs to try the turn on seqeunce in local, but they unfortunately were also no able to get any powerr above 10 kW.Thsi remonded me very much of the BRRF trouble we had when we started this latest user run after the loing SD when Ben had to manually tune up the BRRF to get pwr to cavity. The max gain I can apply is 0.71 and that resulted in 10 kW. Out of despair, I set the gain back to 0.6 and ran BR hwinit. To my surprise, immediately the traces came back up to usual levels and after ramping gain back to 0.68 we were back to 40 kW.

author: operator_1
subject: BBA around LEDA
details: In preparation for a potential GEMINI realignment I checked quad centering around LEDA. Our ops files have for BPMs 1,9 and 2,3 the following goldens originally based on our 2021 realignment: -0.2638/-0.1051 and 0.0556/-0.8669 (before application of our LEDA-specific bump).Went to 65 mA and corrected orbit and tunes. For q19=quadcenter('QF',[1,2],0) I recorded -0.1595/-0.4137 and for q23=quadcenter('QD',[2,1],0) I see 0.0418/-0.7730. Both attached.Further analysis will take place offline.

author: operator_2
subject: New filter setup for BL3.1
details: Changchun and I tested the new filter setting for BL3.1. We were able to get the gain and exposure down significantly (while retaining previous signal amplitude) with the new filter setting. However, a previously almost perfectly round beam then appeared ellioptical and left-right asymmtric with a ~16% aspect ratio. Changchun's suspision that we were too close to the filter edge led us to bump to the beam inboard by 0.5 mm at the source point. With that we immediately saw an almost perfectly round beam with good fit. So the plan now is to ask S&A to realign the beamline accordingly and after that we should be able to transition to the new filter setup. For now, the previous filter and its calibrations/defaults have been restored.

author: operator_2
subject: Spurious beam motion in SR08/9 due to poorly regulating AHU26
details: We have lately observed non-physical orbit deviations in SR08 and SR09 with a period opf many hours. Previously, we had identified AHU26 as showing poor regulation where it goes through large-amplitude oscillations with a period of about 6 hrs.The AHU itself appears to be on and in auto (unlike when AHU20 and AHU21 were discovered off on 4/1), nevertheless AHU26 is showing a regulation much unlike all other AHUs leading to large swings in its supply air temp as a consequence of large oscillatory action on its CHW valve in spite of flat input temp (see attached). The unit AHU26 itself is located in SR09, however, its zone temp sensor is next to B3 in SR08 since that is roughly centered along the duct sock fed by AHU26.Since these large swings are interfering with beam motion/control and BPM readings, and since they persisted for quite a while apparently unaffected by  intervention in early April, it would be nice if FAC would invetsigate and implement a plan to correct for this poor regulation.

details: Under controlled access, the mech techs helped us identify the faulty thermocouple.  The thermocouple connector looked like it might've been bumped and one of the flat pins of the thermocouple connector was pulled out pretty far (see picture).  It would not push back in, so  suggested pulling the connector out and reinserting it.   pulled out the connector and after straightening that pin a little, carefully reinserted as far as it would go.  We called the CR and they confirmed that the EPS screen showed green for TM003.  On our way back, we checked that the temperature monitor at BL0522 had a reasonable reading of 25 deg C.

author: operator_2
subject: BPM(5,11) appears to have broken again - channel D seems low.
details: At 06:33 this morning BPM(5,11) seems to have broken again, such that the orbit values relative to golden were off by ~1mm horizontally and ~3mm vertically. This broke slow orbit FB. A colleague and I removed BPM(5,11) from orbit correction and orbit feedback by hand and successfully restarted orbit feedback. We'll run like this for now so we don't have to interrupt user ops to properly reload the lattice and recorrect the orbit. Ops: important note that the compiled version of SRControl does have BPM(5,11) in the loops, so if for some reason we need to restart SRControl we'll need to take it out by hand again. I will work on recompiling when I get a chance.

author: operator_2
subject: Single Bunch Inj Efficiency
details: Single bunch filling has been poor/unpredicatable over the last few days/ even weeks? Multibunch fill efficiency is also not great. We turned off the single bunch fill after the first mod trip today to reach 500 mA faster. CAM current went down to ~4.24 mA. since then, I have been tuning, from the Linac to the BTS/SR, to try to make single bunch fill and over all efficiency better. At one point, CAM reached 5 mA, but it did not last. Even though the br beam got much better, most shots above 1.8 nC and max above 2.2 nC, CAM current would not reach 5 mA again (currently at ~4.47 mA). I have also tried different combinations of SR SEK and SEN, ~5194 V (was ~5204 V) and ~1785 A (was ~1759 A), at present. SR inj efficiency is below 30% but we are maintaining 500 mA in SR comfortably (single bunch fill is on to fill CAM as much as possible) because of a very strong LTB/BR performace.

author: operator_2
subject: Booster QF Offset change stopped injection
details: After the most recent Mod 2 trip, we were tuning the LTB line to improve the booster beam. The beam was gone completely on the Booster ICT, hence no injection. Troubleshooting started with the linac beam, which looked good in LTB3, and TWE had four bunches, but Booster ICT was flat at zero. Looking at the injection charge monitor, the BR ICT - Turn 1 was showing some charge, but the current was gone for the rest of the BR. Looking at booster waveforms, QFMeasured was off significantly from QFGolden. By looking at the offset (BR1_____QF_PSQFAC00), and gain (BR1_____QF_PSGNAC00), it was realized that the Booster QF gain was inexplicably (instantaneous drop) changed from 0.97 to 0.87 at 10:11 am. The change was not made by someone in the control room, and the root cause is not known. After reverting this value, QFM measured waveform matched QFGolden, which recovered the injection. Now recovering back to 500 mA.

author: operator_4
subject: re log  entry for SR08 superbend temperature alarm
details: This PV (SR08C___BSC_T7_AM06) is an analogue input (ai) record, the value of which originated from the lakeshore controller over GPIB, and arrives via a subarray record (SR08C_BSC_T_SUB7).While the subroutine record is reacting fast to changes, as is seen on the hardware, the ai record reacts 'slowly' the high values when they come only reduce slowly. This is typical behaviour of an AI record with a value set in the SMOO field - which is in effect a low pass filter.But when I looked this morning in the epics database (.db) file, the smooth field was not set - only the HYST field - which should only effect alarms not the value. But what I see now, is although the SMOO field is not set in the database, it is set in the 'live' record and so is causing this behavior.   This SMOO field is being read on startup from autosave, and has perhaps been set from a Matlab setup script, or manually at some time.  So this is (or was) the desired behavior.  PLease let us know if this behavior should be changed.
category: Accelerator Controls, Accelerator Physics, Insertion Device, Operations

author: operator_2
subject: New golden orbit through SR02S
details: Based on the recent V aperture scan we know the beam needs to go low through SR02S. We also know GEMINI wants to see their light go up and inboard. So I used this to push the beam down and take out a little of the angle that we had put in there after the long SD. With a colleague I was able to monitor the change of the spot at GEMINI while bumping through SR02S. The new golden orbit puts the beam u/s of LEDA low by 0.4 mm which is the exact same amount as the recent V aperture scan called for. D/s of LEDA the beam was lowered by 0.2 mm.I recorded new golden orbits for 3 pairs of adjacent BPMs and saved these to our ops code. Recompiled for both CentOS7 and Rocky8. Briefly tested and confirmed all OK in  terms of CMs as well as likely OK in terms of fields at GEMINI and lifetime (hard to say definitely quite yet because the lattice reload at 500 mA took out 170 mA). Will verify later once JH scrapers have been re-set and a fresh machine setup completed.Recorded another V aperture scan with the new golden in 16b mode (attached). Less noisy than last scan and confirmed beam better centered now (would want another 0.2 mm down).

author: operator_1
subject: BR Bump 2 Troubleshooting
details: BR Bump 2 has been having trouble triggering during startup for a couple of shutdowns so far. We went to the back of the BR Bump Magnet Low Level Control Chassis (23W7204, located above BR Bump 2 SCR Power Supply) and wiggled cables one by one to see if we could disable the trigger that way. We were unsuccessful in causing any change to the triggering.Looking at the BR Bump control chassis drawing (23W7204), the BR Extraction Bump Pulser (23W6664), and the BR Bump System Diagram (23W6834), the BR Bump Control Chassis PG17 controls the voltage of the Bump2 SCR Power Supply, while PG6 outputs the trigger for all 3 Bumps. We added stabilant to these connections in hope that it helps in the future.

subject: Injection update
details:
We are maintaining ~500mA in the ring, with both single bunch fillings on and Leda at 5.5mm gap. We are ok but we are right on edge. 
The max inj efficiency is ~28%, after patiently tuning the BTS parameters manually, using the traj feedback to sort of kick the beam into place at intervals (the efficiency was low single digits when I started). LTB and BR parameters were tweaked to make the Linac/BR beam as stable as possible. When we were sure we turned things around, we opened Leda to 8mm so that we can reach 500mA faster in top-off mode. After closing Leda at ~500mA, more BTS tuning was done to turn on the single bunch fillings.
When I started, SR current was down to ~400mA.

subject: Tuning Summary
details: We were not able to tune the Linac at first. It was like MASTPH control has no effect whatsoever even when it went through the whole range. We noticed SHB2 PH readback value was zero. Operator_2 had to put the LLRF chassis into remote. After that MASTPH tuning worked as normal. We had to increase MASTPH value to ~8. The other notable tuning process is the BTS tuning. We had to line up the BTS twice. We had very poor fill rate after the first try. The BTS feedback trajectory would not even run due to low signal. We checked the BTS and found that the beam had moved dramatically. So we decided to line it up again and this time fill rate was slightly better. We ran the orbit correction early on but it did not help bring up the fill rate. We finally achieved over 1mA shots by lowering the SR SEN from ~1760 A to ~1722 A.

author: operator_1
subject: 1700: BL5.3 FVS101 & FVS 102 Troubleshooting
details: There were two issues that were impacting this FV system. FVS101 module has been tripping frequently (in matter of seconds) FVS102 has been spazzing between 10^-8 and 10^-6 Issue #1: The BL5.3 FVS101 module had an issue this winter and as part of troubleshooting,  put in place a new module with the settings that works for this BL But, as we know, with all the umpteen variations of the obsolete FV system designs and hardware,  did not have the exact same version and hence had to replace it with a newer version when  replaced it and work around with the dip switch settings and other modifications, to fit the newer version into the older design chassis It did pass the QA test back then and functioned as expected during operations. But this module is not accepting the "bypass" option now (which was not part of the QA test) We currently do not have qualified spares to replace this module However, this module has not tripped since yesterday, when  worked on it As an added measure,  have increased the "filter" threshold for the sensor, to deal with any small false positives Issue #2: BL 5.3 FVS102 spazzing issue is a typical 'connector - cable shielding' symptom as the voltage spikes between the shielding and the pin in the coax causes a fake high pressure signal  have opened the connector, receded and combed the shielding back in to place and plugged it back in. Did not see any spazzing after this Repeated the QA test and made sure everything is working in place for the BL5.3 FV system. Summary is that the FV system for BL5.3 works as of now. But there is a non-zero chance that this can trip again and if it trips again, we can neither bypass it nor replace it with qualified spares.

author: operator_3
subject: Modified BTS traj FB
details: Watching the beam trajectory through the BTS I had almost convinced myself that the trajectory does not appear to deteriorate after a SB shot. But once I switched the BTS traj FB off entirely, indeed, shots after SB shots no longer showed poor capture in the SR.In response to this observation I have modified the BTS traj FB code. The code now checks if we are injecting MB and only corrects for those shots. When it detects SB shots it skips a FB step and reports that to its console. This is in addition to the previous gating on poor SNR.Modified the code and tested it. It's now again running on the apps3 console. We should observe if this manages to resolve the issue with poor capture after SB shots. If not, we can disable BTS traj FB once again.

subject: SR capture efficiceny dropping after SB shots
details: The attached plot illustrates the observation. The capture efficiency in the SR is the blue trace. author: operator_3
subject: Filter testing for BL31
details: The current carbon filter for BL3.1 is the thickest ones in the filter set. It has pushed the gain and exposure time to their maximum limits at 10 Hz in order to have a good beam size measurement. The thinner filter next to the current one has been tested. With this thinner filter, the camera gain can be reduced from 33 to 20 and the exposure time reduced from 0.095 sec to 0.02 sec, which still provide a plenty of beam signal. However, the measured beam size (55um/49um) are significantly different from the current beam size measurements (46um/46um). This is probably due to different uniformity and the degree of degradation of filters over 30 years operations. We can re-calibrate the measurement if the thinner filter is decided to be used for operations. Here are the beam size measurement and camera setting with these two different filters.

author: operator_1
subject: AutoScrape
details: Was able to test the new autoscrape.m. It has an interactive mode (for use in a MATLAB console) where it asks for the desired current to scrape down to. It also has a non-interactive mode (for use as a compiled app) where it will use the Phoebus AutoScrape target current as its goal.The app scrapes down to the target current fairly quickly and quite reliably. It is deliberately a bit less aggressive than older implementation in an attempt to prevent tripping the overcharge watchdog. In today's testing it indeed never tripped the watchdog, however, I still see BCM report significant amounts of charge appearing in 308. I'll need to think about that some more.For now, the compiled versions are available (compiled for both Centos7 and Rocky8 machines) and so is the interactive version for use from within any MATLAB console initialized to SR.

subject: HiLo lattice cleanup shift
details: Resumed cleanup of the HiLo lattice - in preparation for ALS-U RF bellows test at end of summer shutdown.Switched to 1.9 GeV Top-Off mode in middle layer - this is where the lattice is saved.Cycled lattice using srramp: srramp(1.522,'LinearByEnergy') and srramp(1.89,'LinearByEnergy') - Superbends are slowing down rampLoaded production lattice of Top-Off mode - this is the HiLo latticeAt first did not have any injection. Problem was traced to transfer line. Supposedly this had happened earlier today as well. We had >5 mm trajectory deviations in x and >2 mm in y and the trajectory feedback would not work.  said that earlier today  needed to change BTS B3 by a lot. This time things seemed to be even further off and it required to line up the BTS by hand at least enough to start the trajectory feedback. This was not related to the HiLo lattice, no changes were made top the BTS or pulsed elements when the lattice was loaded.Afterwards, we got many turns, but still low capture efficiency. It turns out the the orbit had drifted since the last time this lattice was used (in November). This also changed the tune. So manually bumped the x tune up by 0.04 - this allowed reasonable injection. However, when trying orbit correction or local bumps, the beam would immediately dump, even with small number of singular values. It seems like the response matrix and BPM configuration has changed enough since November that I needed to measure a new response matrix. This worked, but afterwards I was out of time (only had 1 hour). So will need to restart from here the next time. Symmetry of lattice in response matrix looked OK and tunes were still a bit off, but not too bad. So It should be possible to resume reasonably efficiently the next time.After the response matrix was done, reloaded the user lattice and cycled the lattice. Also reset the BPMs to normal setting with pilot tones on - they were switched to turn-by-turn settings to debug injection challenges.

subject: No obvious correlation with 15-mA beam loss
details: The beam loss was not concurrent with any abrupt ID configuration change (and thus also without any skew changes via ML ID FF, confirmed via DWP). Triggered 3 sec of V beam blowup, and indeed TFBy is showing instances of output saturation during this run. This beam loss occurred between two injection shots, both being multibunch shots (into 96 and 154). No temperature variations. In fact, our hottest flexband (in the SR07 chicane) was running at 95C when the loss occureed, about 10C lower than its usual max. No vacuum signature anywhere - not even an indication of where we dumped the lost charge (unlike during the last event).Although the overall loss was 15 mA and thus very minor on the MB train, the cam lost 0.6 mA, 12% of its entire charge during this event. Cam recovery (once MB had been stabilized at 500 mA) took about 20 min.

author: operator_4
subject: Continuous LN Mod 1 Trips
details: Summary: Yesterday (4/3/24), Modulator 1 was continuously tripping on T&I&0x5CExternalInt1 Input Missing (Reverse Power Trip / Waveguide Arc).  and myself went to troubleshoot why it would not work. At the RF drive power and voltage it was set at, the Mod 1 would always trip right away. In the end, we were able to get Mod 1 to run normally again by cleaning up the RF connections on the Mod 1 RF Distribution chassis (SLAC 239-044), lowering the RF Drive power to a lower level, then slowly increasing the drive power until the power was at a passable level.  helped tremendously with getting this back to a running state.Events: We started at lower RF drive power levels expecting it to fulfill a similar role as conditioning the Modulator. However, the first time we tried slowly increasing the drive power, we got the output to a passable level, but we increased it one more time and it tripped on Reverse Power again. After this trip, we were unable to raise the power to anywhere near its previous value. At this point we continued to other forms of troubleshooting.We connected a scope to the patch panel on LI21, on the points LN AS1 Forward Pwr, LN AS1 Load FWD PWR, LN AS2 Forward Pwr, and LN AS2 Load Fwd Pwr. When arc happened, we expected to see an unexpected waveform come out on this scope, and on the scope connected to the Mod 1 (by its PLC screen). However, all waveforms looked ordinary. This made it look unlikely that arcs were actually happening. We got help from control room and  to look at the PVs related to the trip. It was noticed that there was even a recorded "waveguide arc trip" while Mod1 was not triggering, which further confirmed that the trips were likely false.With the help of , we looked at the Mod 1 RF Distribution Chassis and found no noticeable problems. We cleaned up the connections with stabilant and attempted to raise the modulator power again. Once we got to a point where Control Room could inject, we left it where it was.Note: when changing the RF Drive power, make sure the modulator is not triggering. Demote to HV or lower. When increasing the RF Drive power, the power meter connected to the RF Distribution chassis should be at least 102dBm for Control room to have a chance at injecting. We typically raised the RF Drive power by 0.5-1.5 dBm at a time, then let the Modulator run for a minute or more before increasing again. author: operator_2
subject: Large RF correction needed
details: While operator_1 and company troubleshoot the vac issues in LN Mod1 waveguide, I took a look at the lattice. I was able to confirm the large corrections applied by tune feedback. Also, the main RF appeared very low (usually it's quite a bit higher when we restart after a 2-day outage). Opened the gaps, turned off FBs, and reloaded the lattice. Saw significant CODs. Corrected orbit and this immediately raised the main RF by 325 Hz. OCO resulted in the usual 18 micron rms orbit. Turned FBs back on and tune corrections are all back to normal again.Before turning on FBs, it's important to always verify that orbit correction has completed successfully and resulted in both good orbit and corrected main RF (as detailed in SRcontrol's console output).

author: operator_2
subject: ID9 amp trip investigation
details: I have managed to recreate the amplifier trip on ID 9. The cause is that if a scan is started that is a long way from the current position and the scan does not wait for the first long move to complete before continuing with the scan, there is a bug in the low level software that detects an increasing following error at each step in the scan. Once the following error is above .075 mm, the amplifier will fault. I will be working on finding the bug, but in the meantime the beam line will need to wait until the initial scan position is reached before continuing the scan. I believe they want to do this anyway because the first few scans will not be correct.
category: Accelerator Controls, Beamline Activities, Insertion Device, Operations

author: operator_3
subject: 1530: SE0187 & SE0983 Troubleshooting Findings
details: Original issue:o   SE0187 white lights were not turning on, red lights were okay.o   SE0983 red lights were not turning on, white lights were okay.Troubleshooting:Continuity: SE0187 was dissembled and checked for continuity, there were no continuity issues from connector to the module.Power Supply Check: A power supply was connected to the connector on Pin B to positive and Pin E for negative. Voltage was gradually increased from 0VDC to 20VDC, which produced a soft red light.When Pin A was connected to positive and Pin E for negative, no white light was produced except a bright flash around 40VDC.When measuring across the white LED strip while the power supply is set at 30V, the positive end shows a voltage reading of 29V and the negative end shows 21V.When the same test is applied to SE0983, Pin A & Pin E to the power supply, white light was produced on around 30V.On SE0983, Pin B & Pin E to the power supply, the red strip LED strip shows a reading of 10V on the positive, and 7V on the negative.Module Swap: The L-650 Driver Module was swapped in from the nonfunctional white lights of SE0187 into the functional white lights of SE0983. This would not power on. The L-650 Driver Module was swapped back into SE0983 and was able to light back up.The L-650 Driver Module was swapped in from the functional red lights of SE0187 into the nonfunctional red lights of SE0983. The power supply was able to power on the red lights on SE0983 after this swap. We left this module inside SE0983 and tested for current draw. At 48VDC, the red lights drew 0.384A and the white lights drew 0.892A.Conclusions:The L-650 Driver Module seems to be the main cause of the lighting issues. A swap with a functional driver module should fix the issue. The lighting fixture must be removed from the unistrut and on a level surface to open the fixture to access this driver module. To diagnosis with a power supply, check the voltage between the positive and negative end on the LED strip, where if the negative end would be ~60% - 70% of the applied voltage. A follow-up attachment will be attached later with photos and examples.

author: operator_2
subject: Progress of recovering beam earlier
details: After EMs replaced the quench detection chassis and the mech techs finished topping off SB8 (~1100), we started LN Mod timeouts and ran SB8 up to golden value. (reminder that hardware initialization should be run after turning on SBs) Cylced the SR lattice. LN Mod2 tripped when going to transmit mode, error T&iFiberIntSts Input, which isn't on the list but Revsen found relevant into in an old log entry: May 18, 2023 17:55:43. Will write onto the list.Once we had beam in the LTB and Booster, attemped to fill at about the same time that  noticed the SR SEK trace was flat (our standard graph for that is fairly small and not super obvious showing the problem). Setpoint looked correct but no readback value. Power cycle did not help. Called EMs for assistance. They looked at the supply and determined that the setpoint wasn't being recieved. Called  for help (see his log entry at 13:23:49).When SEK was outputting properly, filling began. SEK did require tuning to improve injection. Reached 108mA stored beam when injection (all injector RF) was lost due to radiation monitor trip at L4 on the SR roof at 12:12. This was due to the integration limit exceeding 10mA for one hour (partially due to  neglecting to put TV paddles in after the SEK problem was identified). Integration cleared at 1218, we reset the rad moitor and turned on all injector RF.This whole time, the LN was jumping, the TV spots never looked great, but was ok. Topoff kept up with 500mA for about 45min. More tuning will definitely improve the situation.

author: operator_4
subject: Adjusted golden orbit through LEDA
details: At 500 mA and after having had all FBs working, I ran bumps through SR02S with operator_1 and we observed light at the YAG d/s of his mono (with LEDA at 8 mm). Running small angle bumps and slight V translation allowed us to both improve alignment in the beamline as well as reduce CM excitation in at least two locations around LEDA. This would support that 2,1 was moved during the recent BTA kicker installation. Since the changes are small (for 1,10 and 2,1 +0.2/-0.1 in the V and +0.075/-0.075 in the H) and we see CM excitation in this area closer to where we were during the last user run, I'm electing to for now keep this bump in our golden orbit. Recompiled srcontrol and plotfamily. Restarted these apps, corrected orbit, and ran all FBs. All good.
