author: operator_4
subject: Machine Setup
details: Scraped down to 60 mA (using MATLAB AutoScrape.m), loaded lattice, corrected orbit to 17/22 microns rms. BPMs to low current mode. Measured ORM. LOCO converged after 3 iterations to 2.86 microns rms of measured (1 outlier) with chi^2/DOF = 21.695. 3% beta beat.Symmetrized and corrected coupling. BPMs back to user mode. OCO to 15/22 microns rms of golden and tunes at 0.159/0.256. Checked all CMs good. Saved golden.Cycled. Injected to 60 mA. OCO to 15/21 microns rms of golden. Corrected tunes 0.1567/0.2590 –> 0.1603/0.2499. Saved new golden lattice.Injected to 500 mA with all FBs. At 500 mA in topoff measured BL31 beam sizes 45.5/47.3 microns rms. Corrected (-0.0422 on skew wave) to 45.7 microns rms. Lifetime is 5.5 hrs. Closed 5W and measured 45.3/46.1 microns rms with lifetime 5.1 hrs. Compared to last Tue (3.6 hrs with just 5W closed), scrubbing and sublimation in SR01/02 helped a lot. SR capture efficiency is 58%. Saved new golden skews (to MML, feedback script, and new skew IOC). Verified BSC recorded offsets. Adjusted its target V beam size to 46.5 microns. Closed all IDs to user gaps. Measured 45.1/44.1 microns rms and 4.2 hrs lifetime. SR capture eff now at 23%. Measured chroma with only 5W closed as 1.27/1.56. All done.

subject: BL 5.3.1 FVS problems
details: Could not get the BL 5.3.1 FV to stay open and ready. FVS102 keeps tripping before we even have a chance to open PS and PSS. Tried resetting at least a dozen times, FVS102 trips either immediately upon resetting BL 5.3.1 EPS or shortly after. Sometimes FV will stay open and ready for a few seconds, but not longer. This happens even if VVR001 and VVR101 are closed and pressures are good. IG103 is the ion gauge at the FVS102 location; pressure on IG103 has been about 3e-8 all afternoon. It does not seem to change when FVS102 trips.We have gone back to 500mA top-off operation while we try to reach the vacuum group for guidance. Low-current scrubbing on 5.3.1 may be able to take place later tonight if we can find a solution or bypass this FVS.

subject: Machine Setup
details: Injected to 60 mA, corrected orbit to 15/21 microns rms. BPMs to low current mode. Measured ORM. LOCO converged after 3 iterations to 2.83 microns rms of measured (3 outlier) with chi^2/DOF = 27.672. <5% beta beat.Symmetrized and corrected coupling. BPMs back to user mode. OCO to 15/22 microns rms of golden and tunes corrected to 0.160/0.250. Checked all CMs good. Saved golden.Cycled. Injected to 60 mA. OCO to 15/22 microns rms of golden. Corrected tunes 0.1499/0.2479 –> 0.1612/0.2504. Saved new golden lattice.Injected to 500 mA with all FBs. At 500 mA in topoff measured BL31 beam sizes 45.6/47.6 microns rms. Corrected (-0.0424 on skew wave) to 45.8 microns rms. Lifetime is 4.1 hrs. Closed 5W and measured 45.4/46.4 microns rms with lifetime 3.6 hrs. Saved new golden skews (to MML, feedback script, and new skew IOC). Verified BSC recorded offsets. Adjusted its target V beam size to 46.0 microns. Closed all IDs to user gaps. Measured 44.9/43.3 microns rms (needed to raise TFBY shift gain 3–>4 to maintain stability) and 1.8 hrs lifetime. Measured chroma with only 5W closed as 1.24/1.51. All done.

subject: SRRF phase adjusted
details: With some more work on the TFB/LFB and some manual tune adjustments we were able to tune the SRRF master phase SP to maximize capture efficiency in the SR and minimize the synchr oscillations we see on the TxT BPM data (see attahced). The resulting SRRF master ph SP is now -246 deg (-101 deg on loop2) which correpsonds to a VVM reference of about -93 deg for ops well below 200 mA. This matches the new BRRF phase SP of +60 deg. author: operator_1
subject: Adjusted BRRF and SRRF phases
details: We had previously bumped up against the limit of the BRRF phase shifter (0-180 eg) so today we asked a technician to remove a piece of extension cable (~ 30 cm) on the BRRF. After they had removed the cable we adjusted the BRRF phase SP to maximize capture into the booster and minimize shot-to-shot variation. We ended up with a BRRF phase SP of +60 deg.With this in place we set out to adjust the SRRF master phase SP. Capture into the SR was very low making it hard to observe anything, so I adjusted the SEN (we cannot presently tune SEK through EPICS). This made a huge difference. I ended up adjustiung it from 1748 to 1778 which also dropped rad monitor readings quite a bit. We moved the SRRF master ph SP by small amounts while taking care not to lose phase lock. But in spite of scraping to low current a couple of times, we ran into MB stability issues. I see slightly lower synchr oscillations on the sum TxT BPM signal with SRRF phase adjusted from -216 to -226 and this also gets us to almnost 50% capture (~0.6 mA/shot), but it's not clear that this is yet optimal. And I lose MB stability at anything lower. Pushing the phase to the other side does not appear to reduce synch oscillations or improve capture.Further investigation of the SRRF phase would be necessary. But for now I'm not even leaving in the -10 deg adjutsment I want because we are so marginal in terms of MB stability. Will revisit when we can tune up the TFB/LFB. Otherwise, for now the new SRRF master ph SP would be set to -226 deg (= -58 deg compared to last user run) corresponding to a VVM SP of -65 deg for ops below 200 mA.

subject: 500 mA topoff established
details: We filled with all FBs running and reached 500 mA where we went into topoff. All pressures look ok, the transverse spectra show clear signs of ions (attached). Initial lifetime is 2.8 hrs at 500 mA. Capture into the SR at the moment is a bit jumpy, but about 0.5 mA/shot on average. author: operator_1
subject: All FBs running
details: I removed BPM 2,1 from our orbit correction configs since that BPM first needs a new golden (it was moved when the BTA kicker was installed). But with that BPM out, all orbit correction with the usual SV count worked just fine. I also see no orbit deviations in the SR02C area where the dipole was removed. Checked CM excitations and found nothing too egregious. I reconfigured FOFB and launched all OFBs. No problems. I'll continue to observe for CM drift.After  tweaked the LFB and phase loop some more, we were able to launch the slow phase FB (using a new -58 deg for the VVM reference below 200 mA). Phase servo delta has been kept at zero all the way to and beyond 450 mA.With the TFB/LFB established well enough, we see nice notches on both transverse spectra. With that established, we we able to start tune FB. No oddness observed there either.With this we now have all FBs running, and injection continues as we just crossed 480 mA.

author: operator_2
subject: Saved lattice at 300 mA
details: We have injected up to 300 mA now. In the meantime we moved the SRRF phase by the same -50 deg we had moved the BRRF phase and that (-218 deg on master ph SP) allowed us to get rid of almost all the synchr oscillation we saw on the TxT BPM sum signal. We nudged the tunes slighlty by hand (less than 0.01 in either plane) and corrected the orbit by hand (127 SVs, ToF config mostly). Even with this new SRRF phase and despite the phase servo being railed we are multibunch stable ( did a manual tweak of the LFB FE phase). We saved a new golden lattice. No unusual heating observed anywhere (<1C on the BTA kicker ceramic), pressures stable with 2e-8 the highest (SR02C-IG2) apart from inj straight (3e-8).

author: operator_3
subject: Stored 10 mA beam
details: After some hand tuning of the new PS for the SEK we managed to inject about 2 mA. This confirmed that in spite of a -50 deg change in BRRF phase, we are still within the wide (~200 deg) SRRF phase acceptance (SRRF master ph restored at -168 deg). This small amount of beam allowed us to get rid of the dispersion (+4 kHz on main RF) and correct the orbit. From there on we were able to stack more quickly (~0.4 mA/shot) and we arrived at ~ 10 mA where we paused injection to observe temperatures (nothing observed around BTA kicker) and pressures (mainly SR02C-IG2 from 4e-9 to 2e-8). Performed several more iterations of orbit correction at gradually increased no. of SVs, but eventually lost beam when we called for too much VCM strength in SR01. Interrupted running beam for BRRF cable repair.

author: operator_4
subject: Temporary installation for SR SEK power supply.
details: We have a temporary power supply installed for the SR SEK. It currently sits on a stand next to the usual racks, and is only locally operable at this time.The present setpoint that allowed injection into the SR is 5.18 kV, as read on the right-hand display.There is a Control Lock button which should be engaged unless actively tuning the voltage with the right-hand knob.It is quite sensitive - the difference between injection and no injection was a couple 1/100ths of a kV. The knob itself is also sensitive and there is no voltage limit for the 10kV supply at the moment, so we need to be VERY CAREFUL not to set the voltage too high. 5.5kV should still be okay, but do not go above that under any circumstances. There should be no need since even going as high as 5.25 killed injection completely. When the supply is pulsing, read the value as it temporarily pauses at its maximum (see attached video to see what it looks like.)

author: operator_2
subject: Thick septum / Glassmann PS troubleshooting
details: Delayed Report:On Sunday, the 17th, Technician and I embarked on resolving issues with the Thick septum due to a recent detection of a burnt smell. Upon initial inspection of the pulser chassis, we determined it to be in good condition. Upon requesting CR to activate the PS, we observed that it failed to turn on during the first two attempts. However, on the third attempt, the chassis began pulsing loudly, indicating suspected arcing. Concurrently, the lights in other elements of the same rack were affected, presumably due to a power surge from the PS. We promptly powered it off and identified the Glassmann PS as the source of the problem.Upon opening the PS chassis, we discovered signs of arcing and internal burning in the HV PS (photos attached). Unfortunately, the spare we located required some adaptation. We needed to modify an analog DB25 connector for the new unit, and the 208V power cord and the HV cable's tip length were incompatible with the new PS.On Monday, the 18th, we located the socket for the power cord and successfully connected the PS. Engineer crafted a new HV cable, but despite testing with Colleague 1, Colleague 2, and Colleague 3, we were unable to use the remote control signals. Colleague 4 suggested operating the PS in local mode and proceeding with system tuning.Further troubleshooting will be conducted by Colleague 1 and the Controls team to explore enabling Ethernet control instead of analog control.

author: operator_1
subject: BRRF phase optimized for BR transmission
details: We do not yet have SRRF, but I was able to check the BRRF phase as a function of transmission through the BR. Our long-standing BRRF phase SP has been +50 deg. Presently (with about 4 nC on the LTB-ICT) that gives us at best about 0.2 nC at the end of the BR ramp and there is a lot of shot-to-shot fluctuation. But if I lower the BRRF phase SP to 0.0 deg (read-back is +3 deg), I see up to 0.8 nC at the end of the BR ramp and the shot-to-shot variation is substantially better. Our BRRF phase control is limited to [0:180] so I'm not convinced the new 0-deg SP is actually optimal. Would be good to add 180 deg (at 500 MHz) of cable and revisit (especially before we retune the SRRF master phase SP).

author: operator_2
subject: Booster sextupole ramping
details: When the booster sextupoles were turned on after the long shutdown, the triggering of the ramping waveforms was off.  Each of the miniIOCs gets a trigger from a very old trigger distribution system so I thought one of those systems might have partially failed.  On inspection there is an odd Burndy connector on the chassis in the B0202 rack which has 2 resistors soldered to pins but are just hanging in the air.  The two resistors were touching each other.  When I separated them the booster sextupole waveforms returned to normal.

author: operator_2
subject: 2145: SR5 PST Vent Sol issue
details: While doing EPS testing on , I noticed that the switches on the 24V Power Distr Chassis in rack S0515 had a couple switches turned ON and the LEDs OFF, indicating blown fuses. I turned the switches OFF and did not stop my work to address it. On Monday evening, I reached out to EMs and went in to the pit for troubleshooting. When we replaced the fuses, it blew again as soon as we turn the switch ON. I was able to narrow the fault down to the the "PST vent" solonoid on 23W891. Since SR needs controlled access and was not planned to take beam that night anyway and it was late in the night, we decided to postpone further inspections to the next morning to understand it better and see if it could impact operations. I left the solonoid disconnected at S051555x-13A, taped up.After talking to , we agreed that this will not impact operations and that we can address it on the first 2day shutdown to not impact starup schedule.

subject: LN Solenoid magnets - Interlock Test
details: The Interlock chain for LN Solenoid magnets has been successfully tested. Scope of the test was to check the effectiveness of the modifications made. In the old system (with old TCR power supplies), said interlock chain was managed by the LN Control Chassis (23W1215). The modification provided didn't change anything in the interlock chain, but redesigned the interface with the new power supplies (TDK Lambda Genesys+).

author: operator_3
subject: Sector 4 PLC follow up
details: Following up on the issue with the sector 4 PLC that seemingly rebooted itself last December and caused a beam dumpThe last status was that the PLC controller and power supply were replaced but there were 3 EPICS PVs that still reported "READ ALARM" and couldn't communicate with the PLC. As you can see in the attachment, the READ ALARM started right around when the beam dumped and the PLC rebooted.I found that the reason the PVs were not working is that the PLC tags for these PVs were missing in the PLC. In fact, it appears as though the PLC program running was a previous version from at least 9 years ago. You can see when the tags/PVs were changed by  here - https://git.als.lbl.gov/accelerator-controls/epics/iocs/siocsxintlk/-/commit/7bf8449f9fd4306dbe89e502521d3663cee519c4#0a79ba5301d51bd86c62c3635fca464575e27da3_902_902Still need to investigate more but for now, reloading the latest L5X file from git fixed the PV connection issues. It seems like the PLC rebooted/crashed and booted back with an older version of the program. The PLC has an SD card to keep backups of the programs but I don't know how a power disruption or crash would cause this.
category: Accelerator Controls, EPS, Electronics Maintenance, Operations, Power Supplies

details: We have replaced the X-ray transmissive window for BL8.0.1.4 (wetRIXS) endstation at the location in front of vacuum chamber. The following steps were performed:1. Lock-close VVR124 (als-floorops)2. Close VVR125 (generic_person - )3. Vent wetRIXS (8.0.1.4) endstation4. Replace X-ray transmissive window from current Si3N4 to SiC membrane window (to allow user groups to measure N K-edge XAS starting from March 2024)5. Pump down wetRIXS (8.0.1.4) endstationThe vacuum pressure in wetRIXS (8.0.1.4) endstation is now lower than 9x 10^-9 torr. So, we now request unlock VV124.

author: operator_2
subject: Water leak above BL 7.0.1.1
details: Staff from another beamline reported a water puddle in BL 7.0 area. I found a large puddle in 7.0.1.1 endstation and user area. Located the source above 7.0.1.1 endstation, a leaking valve or fitting on manifold appears to be BL LCW. First two photos show source of leak. It was leaking onto power circuits and electronics on endstation but I was able to safely secure the water by closing valves.  These supplied equipment in overhead in last photo. Not sure what that equipment is but leak was causing an immediate safety hazard.There is a large puddle in BL 7.0.1.1. I will notify PMTs but not sure what access is needed this weekend. If BL staff want to come to check equipment in please call control room and I will send a more urgent request for facilities to help mop up.

author: operator_4
subject: Bucket Loader Mode
details: We were asked by EMs to enable triggers for pulsed magnet testing. We used the bucket loader, but the status didn't change after clicking RUN. The status switched to RUNNING and STOPPED immediately after. We then noticed that the Bucket Loader Mode Readback value (bucket:mode:rb) was set to SINGLE, which explained the quick change. When we tried to toggle the mode to TABLE, it also did not work. PV info flagged an error: "Error in EPICS Channel Finder Query", so I tried using caget and caput to force the readback value to TABLE. Here is what I ran (output simplified): caget bucket:mode:cmdTABLEcaget bucket:mode:rb SINGLEcaput bucket:mode:rb TABLEold: SINGLEnew: TABLEAfter which we were able to run the bucket loader. I am speculating the problem is with the channel finder, and reporting the mismatch here. I reversed the changes I made, except now the rb and cmd values are both set to SINGLE

subject: Issues connecting to bastion hosts
details: In the past two weeks, the control bastion hosts (access-ctrl1 and access-ctrl2) & the development bastion hosts (access-devl1 and access-devl2) have all had hardware refreshes. As a result, their SSH host keys have changed. Due to this, many users may run into an vague and unhelpful error when trying to use any of the bastions as a jump host OR when using the connectALS scripts   ssh -J access-ctrl2.als.lbl.gov appsdev2.als.lbl.gov   kex_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host   Connection closed by UNKNOWN port 65535To verify if you're having this issue, connect directly to the bastion host via ssh:    ssh access-ctrl2.als.lbl.govThe error message you'll encounter should be something along the lines of@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@    WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!     @@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@IT IS POSSIBLE THAT SOMEONE IS DOING SOMETHING NASTY!Someone could be eavesdropping on you right now (man-in-the-middle attack)!It is also possible that a host key has just been changed.The fingerprint for the ED25519 key sent by the remote host isSHA256:G2uB/9OkzWERSrbZUiAEtw78Atgjw6TvClFTg4N2g3k.Please contact your system administrator.Add correct host key in /home/user/.ssh/known_hosts to get rid of this message.Offending ECDSA key in /home/user/.ssh/known_hosts:336  remove with:  ssh-keygen -f '/home/user/.ssh/known_hosts' -R 'access-ctrl2.als.lbl.gov'Host key for access-ctrl1.als.lbl.gov has changed and you have requested strict checking.Host key verification failed.To remedy this, run the command listed in the output above    ssh-keygen -R <hostname>Alternatively, you can either remove/rename your known hosts file at ~/.ssh/known_hosts (not recommended unless nothing else workrs!) or edit the file by hand to delete the lines where the old host key used to be.If the above is not the issue you are facing, pleaes contact als-unix@lbl.gov with the host you're trying to connect to along with a description/screenshot of the error message.Note: access-ctrl1 is still experiencing an outage due to a hardware fault. All ALS control machine connections should go through access-ctrl2 for the time being.

author: operator_2
subject: Radiation Monitor PVs
details:
Hi All,Were are making new EPICS PVs for the gamma radiation monitors active. These are both to read values in RPIX and values read directly into EPICS from the monitors.Note the monitors provide data both into EPICS and RPIX every 4 seconds, in units of mRem/hour but only with a resolution of 1mRem/hour !!!! so the typical raw data is either 0 or 1 when radiation is low. So this is only usefull when averaged over a longer period.From RPIX we get the 12 second and 1 hour average dose rates in units of mRem/hr. These are calibrated values (calibration done whenever there is no beam in the mahine), background and injected test signal from the monitors are subtracted. We also integrate in EPICS the reading from RPIX to give a 24 hour integrated dose.The direct EPICS channels are 4 second (uncalibrated) , 12 second, 1 Minute, and 1 Hour average dose rates in units of mRem/hr These are calibrated values (calibration done every short shutdown), so background and injected test signals from the monitors are subracted. The raw (uncalibrated) values are also available. We also integrate the readings to give a 24hour dose.For both RPix and EPICS values we will provide 7 day and 14 day integrated dose readings - this is under test and will require a new host machine that is not rebooted in short shhutdowns.We also have PVs for Neutron measurements, but at the moment not all PVs and only direct EPICS readings. the system will be extended to all values once we are happy with the Gamma.So ... what is available ???

BL2L1: BL2L2: BL2L3: BL4L1: BL4L3: BL5L1: BL5L2: BL6L1: BL6L2: BL7L1: BL7L2: BL8L1: BL8L2: BL8L3: BL8L4: BL8L5: BL9L1: BL9L2: BL10L1: BL11L1: BL11L2: BL12L1: BL12L2: BL12L3: BRL1: BRL2: SRL4: BRL5: BRL6: BRL7: SRL9: SRL10: SRL11: SRL12

Note some monitors are currently off due to shutdown work.

The example PV names are :
EPICS reading RPIX:BL2L1:Gamma:DoseRate - 12 seconds average dose rate
BL2L1:Gamma:DoseRate:Hourly - 1 hour average dose rate (same as 1 hour dose obviously)
BL2L1:Gamma:RpixDose:24Hour - 24 hour integrated dose in units of mRem

EPICS reading monitors directly;
BL2L1:Gamma:DoseRateAvg:4Seconds - 4 second average dose rate (uncalibrated) - resolution of 1mRem
BL2L1:Gamma:DoseRateAvg:12Seconds - 12 second average dose rate (calibrated) - so resolution of 0.333mRem
BL2L1:Gamma:DoseRateAvg:12SecondsRaw - 12 second average dose rate (un-calibrated) not very useful due to noise
BL2L1:Gamma:DoseRateAvg:1Minute - 1 minute average dose rate (calibrated) - updated every 4 seconds with rolling average of the last 15 (4 second) values.
BL2L1:Gamma:DoseRateAvg:1MinuteRaw - minute average dose rate (un-calibrated)
BL2L1:Gamma:DoseRateAvg:1Hour- 1 hour average dose rate (calibrated) - updated every 4 seconds seconds with rolling average of the last 900 (4 second) values.
BL2L1:Gamma:DoseRateAvg:1HourRaw - minute average dose rate (un-calibrated)
BL2L1:Gamma:Dose:24Hour - 24 hour integrated dose (calibrated)
BL2L1:Gamma:Dose:24HourRaw - 24 integrated dose (uncalibrated)

All of these readings are (should be) in the archiver

Note - calibration values can be read in the B field of each PV - for instance BL2L1:Gamma:DoseRateAvg:1Hour.B
Calibration for the EPICS channels is normally done only at every shutdown, doing every time we loose the beam can cause issues (compare EPICS and RPIX 1 hour values in a shutdown)

Some basic phoebus screens are available, but your feedback is needed as to what screens are wanted.

Please try these channels at let us know of any issues or comments.
category: Accelerator Controls, Accelerator Physics, Operations, Radiation

author: operator_1
subject: Glassman HV Power Supply
details: The spare Glassman HV Power Supply was already installed in the rack when I arrived at the beginning of swing shift. After removing LOTO and energizing the power supply, CR notified us that it seems like the Glassman HV PS is still in LOCAL mode because despite changing values on the setpoint, the traces seems to be staying in the same amplitude. We decided to de-energize the Glassman power supply because we noticed from the defective unit that there were jumpers installed between TB1-TB2, and TB8-TB9 only. The spare supply installed in the rack had additional jumpers installed between TB2-TB3, TB5-TB6, and TB10-TB11. After careful reading of the manual for the power supply, it was determined that jumpers were only needed on TB1-TB2, and TB8-TB9 only. We removed the extra jumpers installed in the spare unit and decided to energize the power supply. CR noticed right away the change in amplitude of the traces when they changed values of the setpoint. BR SEK (Thick Septum) started working normally after the extra jumpers were removed.IN: N162136-03AP 060912OUT: N162136-01AP 060912

author: operator_2
subject: SRRF Klystron 2 Rev Pwr
details: Late Log EntryThe trip events were caused by Klystron 2 output operating very close to the trip point (1.5 kW).Mitigation StepsTo address this issue and protect Klystron 2, the SRRF system operation was switched from Dual Mode to Single Klystron 1 Mode. This allowed us to isolate the problem without significantly impacting operations.TroubleshootingCirculator 2 Mismatch AnalysisAfter reviewing the data, the issue was associated with a mismatch in Circulator 2. This could stem from various factors, including:Temperature Control Unit (TCU) calibration issues.Circulator performance degradation.Load problems in Circulator 2.1. Circulator 2 Load InvestigationUpon analyzing data, we found that under worst-case operating conditions, where maximum reflected power would occur, the system should have tripped. However, during full beam operation, where a few kW of reflected power was sent to the dump load, the system tripped.This behavior suggests the issue is less likely to stem from the load and more likely related to the Circulator 2 / TCU combination or another related component.2. Circulator 2 Component InspectionWater Pipes, Coil, and Temperatures:Historical data for temperature and flow Process Variables (PVs) for Circulator 2 showed stable values over the past month.Circulator 2 contains two windings (upper and lower), connected in series with consistent impedance (~53 ohms each).Temperature connections were verified as properly installed and secure.3. Temperature Control Unit (TCU) VerificationConfiguration Files:We compared current configuration files with those from January 2020. Both were identical, confirming no memory issues in the TCU.Testing with Klystron2 with Dummy Load Mode:Klystron 2 was operated in Dummy Load Mode to gather compiled data for the TCU. This data was sent to the vendor for further analysis.ConclusionsKlystron2 with Dummy Load Mode Testing:This mode allows testing of Klystron 2 and Circulator 2 through a magic tee connected to two dummy loads. This configuration ensures a downstream broadband match, effectively removing the effects of the RF cavities during testing.Findings:The return loss at Port 1 of Circulator 2 has degraded. In 2020, it measured ~32 dB after calibration with AFT. It has now decreased to ~19–20 dB, as confirmed by measurements (refer to the spreadsheet in the shared folder).RecommendationsAdjust the EDTO parameter for the TCU to a negative value (e.g., -0.2) for the TOut offset.Reduce the dT Pot setting to zero to remove the high-power compensation portion of the algorithm.These adjustments aim to improve system performance and mitigate the risk of future trip events.More information about the test data in this link
category: Accelerator Physics, Electronics Maintenance, Operations, RF

author: operator_2
subject: Lubricate and Inspect SRRF Cavity 1 and 2 Tuner mechanism
details: Late Log EntryAs part of our efforts to verify the mechanical functionality of the system, we collaborated with a mechanical technician who assisted us during the inspection process.1. Belt Condition CheckWe inspected the condition of the belts for both cavities and found no signs of wear or damage.2. Screw Assembly MaintenanceThe screw assembly was in better condition compared to previous inspections but still showed remnants of old grease, which had hardened significantly. The old grease was removed, and the assembly was thoroughly re-greased to restore optimal performance.3. Tuner Movement TestingUsing the 500 MHz Cavity Phase Tuner Servo Controller Chassis for Cavity 1 and Cavity 2, movement tests were conducted by opening the control loop and manually adjusting the tuner position.Initial Test for Both Cavities:The tuner mechanism did not jam but exhibited very slow movement during the first operation.Resolution for Both Cavities:After lowering and raising the tuner, removing the hardened old grease, and applying new grease, the mechanism moved freely across its full range of motion. This process was repeated several times to ensure consistent and smooth operation.4. Startup ConfigurationFollowing maintenance, both cavities were tuned and adjusted during startup to achieve optimal reverse power levels and proper cavity alignment.ObservationsIn both cavities, the presence of hardened old grease was identified as the primary issue impeding tuner movement.The cleaning and re-greasing process restored full functionality, allowing the tuner mechanisms to operate smoothly across their entire range of motion.This maintenance ensured optimal mechanical performance and alignment for continued operation.
category: Accelerator Controls, Accelerator Physics, Electronics Maintenance, Operations, RF

author: operator_1
subject: Injection Troubles
details: KI2 tripped twice, after running ~30 minutes each time, on overcurrent. technician_1 and technicians investigated, and currently have KI2 in local control. With KI2 in local we were able to close shutters and refill SR before we dropped below 250mA, but while topoff kept up with close to 450mA goal current at first, it's struggling again. KI2 troubleshooting is ongoing.Beam is consistently making it through the first 1000 BR turns, per Injection Charge Monitor, but is often lost by the end of the ramp. Injection is struggling due to not being able to get beam all the way through the booster. Have been trying different save files' QF and QD offsets and gains, but nothing seems to perform well without continuously running BR tuning mode.

author: operator_2
subject: Reconfigured working point in golden lattice
details: Started by nudging tunes in golden lattice 0.16–>0.175. Corrected orbit (17/16 um rms), checked CMs ok, saved golden lattice. In SRcontrol, adjusted nux to 0.18 for tune FB and removed 0.5 de-gain factor on LEDA tune FF. Then on TFBx adjusted filter set 0 for 0.18 tune and reloaded filter. Did NOT save a new s/r config.With these changes in place we were able to run all OFBs and run 480 mA (kly1-only ops) topoff just fine with LEDA closed. Recompiled SRcontrol.At BL3.1 note that beam spot is now fairly well centered after yesterday's strut fastening and today's adjustments to sensor stages.Quick spot check with at 480 mA:Only 5W closed: 48±5% capture, 3.8±0.1 hrs lifetime, 267 kWUser gaps & LEDA 28 mm: 45±5% capture 3.4±0.2 hrs, 277 kWLEDA 8 mm: 40±5% capture, 3.4±0.1 hrsLEDA 5.5 mm: 33±5% capture, 2.8±0.1 hrsLEDA 5.5 mm with local SQ FF running: 33±5% capture, 2.8±0.1 hrs, and residual sigma_y variation ~0.2 um rms at BL3.1With 2.8 hrs lifetime and ≥0.68 mA/shot into the SR, we should be able to maintain topoff 450 mA (Since the local SQ FF does not show any adverse effect on lifetime or capture, decided to leave it in. It relies on the LOCO-derived individual skew fits to the local flanking pair, without any fudge factors. Verified ML ID FF and LEDA local SQ FF do not interfere with one other: the ML ID FF shows very little transient when LEDA closes so ML retraining is not seeing much residual beam size variation when the local FF is running.Returned LEDA to 8 mm gap and adjusted watchdog to enforce 8 mm gap until RA properly established tomorrow. Going into users.

author: operator_1
subject: Booster Injection Kicker 1
details: As said in the previous log, the injection kicker 1 tube and power supply was not the problem. An engineer remembered there were issues with a certain relay in the past and found that part of the left shorting resistor and inductor was broken, and repaired it. We also decided to take a look inside the Booster tunnel, and found that the kicker 1 peaking capacitor had burn marks on the bottom. After cleaning it up and replacing the capacitor, the system was able to work correctly.It is unknown if the relay was a part of the problem or notDo note, we also added kapton tape under both of the peaking capacitors to hopefully help prevent more shorting in the future.

author: operator_1
subject: BL 10.3 front end leak
details: From Tuesday 12/17/2024 We were informed that there was a leak on BL 10.3 Aperature, front end WFS 2B. We located the initial leak which had been pinched off on either side of the leak on the return end. We advise that supply side be pinched first in order to keep supply pressure, around 120 psi, off item being cooled versus return pressure of 36 ish psi.We went to the control room to inform we would be shutting off water to SR 10 girder and because there is some cross connection somewhere with the SR 09 girder, we would also be shtting off water to SR09 girder.Upon return we noticed water spraying from another hose from WFS 1A circuit that was in series with PS1 and a flange between VVR1 and a bellows.Both hoses with leaks were replaced. We did notice that there were some cracks in local hoses so those were replaced as well. Not uncommon unfortunately for all the front ends.Water was returned without issue.

author: operator_3
subject: BR KI troubleshooting
details: EM and I reset and turned on the booster Injection Kickers again individually to see which one is tripping on overcurrent. We identified that it is KI1. After resetting again for overcurrent and turning it on we got a thyratron fault. Again we were able to reset and I put the setpoint very low to try to raise it up very slowly. Our usual setpoint is 97 but the EM observed high current at around 19 and it tripped.We are planning to swap the tube out for KI1 via controlled access once we have a second EM on site which we expect to be around 4AM.

author: operator_4
subject: HV DIS-CONNECT SW SYS Fault
details: Late log entryThe SR HVPS tripped due to a fault in the SR HV Dis-Connect Switch. Upon further investigation, we discovered a desaturation fault in the HV (IGBT) Switch Board located in slot #23, which was observed on the HV (IGBT) Switch Receiver chassis. This is the second failure of this board in a single day.To resolve the issue, we divided the diagnostics into two parts:Voltage Verification: Checking that the input voltages to the board are within acceptable ranges, from the Audio Amplifier to the internal voltages of the board.Wire Test: Verifying that the system response times are within acceptable ranges and determining if the fault is consistent with the system or isolated to the board.Measured Voltages:Audio Amplifier: Output VAC: 40.1VHV (IGBT) Switch Board #23:TP3: ~5VTP9: ~26VTP5: ~18VAll measured voltages were within the correct ranges.Wire Test Results:After conducting multiple wire tests, we confirmed that the board in slot #23 (Board #23) responded prematurely, ahead of the expected timing of the HV Dis-Connect System. We also tested Board #2, which had previously been repaired, but it failed the wire test as well.Action Taken:We replaced the board in slot #23 with a spare. The following changes were made:OUT Board: #23 → IN Board: #41Next Steps:Both boards, #23 and #2, need to be thoroughly inspected and tested before being added back to the spare pool.It must be determined if this error is recurrent across all boards to take corrective actions for the entire batch.Team Involved:Lead: operator_4Assistance: operator_5, operator_6, operator_7, operator_8

author: operator_2
subject: Test of lifetime and injection with diff lattices - LEDA
details: Several tests were conducted to evaluate the feasibility of maintaining a 5.5 mm LEDA gap and 500 mA in top-off mode. Two lattice conditions showed promise: 1) a Pseudo single bunch mode lattice with adjusted nux and increased empirical factor for horizontal tune compensation, and 2) a low emittance lattice with specific nux and nuy values. The results indicate that it may be possible to achieve the desired parameters, but further study is needed to optimize the process.

author: operator_1
subject: LEDA local SQ FF implemented and tested
details: Using the previously established scaling factors for the local SQSHF pair flanking LEDA, I implemented a simple FF that checks if LEDA gap has changed, and when it has, it adjusts the local skew quads to compensate for the change in local (linear) coupling. The script prints to console what it's doing as a heartbeat.The script can be found on the SR path at LEDA_local_SQ_FF.mThere's also a simple script LEDA_local_SQ_fix.m to restore the current golden values to the local skews. This can be useful after bailing out of the FF.Tested both scripts and both appear to be doing what they should.

subject: LEDA local SQ compensation studies
details: Took baseline with all gaps open except for 5W (and SB shots off):LEDA 28 mm: BL3.1 sigma_y = 36.25 um, 37% SR capture, 4.3±0.1 hrs lifetime, 0.6 mr/h on Portables 1 Gamma 3LEDA 16 mm: sigma_y = 36.55 um, 38% SR capture, 4.1±0.1 hrs lifetime, 0.6 mr/h    and with 94% of golden on local SQ: sigma_y = 36.28 um, 39% SR capture, 4.1±0.1 hrs lifetime, 0.6 mr/hLEDA 14 mm: sigma_y = 36.69 um, 37% SR capture, 4.2±0.1 hrs lifetime, 0.6 mr/h    and with 87% of golden on local SQ: sigma_y = 36.26 um, 33% SR capture, 4.3±0.1 hrs lifetime, 0.6 mr/hLEDA 12 mm: sigma_y = 37.04 um, 35% SR capture, 4.3±0.1 hrs lifetime, 0.6 mr/h    and with 82% of golden on local SQ: sigma_y = 36.23 um, 37% SR capture, 4.1±0.1 hrs lifetime, 0.6 mr/hLEDA 10 mm: sigma_y = 37.39 um, 35% SR capture, 4.2±0.1 hrs lifetime, 0.6 mr/h    and with 74% of golden on local SQ: sigma_y = 36.25 um, 35% SR capture, 4.2±0.1 hrs lifetime, 0.6 mr/hLEDA  8 mm: sigma_y = 38.14 um, 36% SR capture, 4.2±0.1 hrs lifetime, 1.2 mr/h    and with 58% of golden on local SQ: sigma_y = 36.26 um, 34% SR capture, 4.0±0.1 hrs lifetime, 1.2 mr/hLEDA  6 mm: sigma_y = 39.27 um, 23% SR capture, 3.6±0.1 hrs lifetime, 2.8 mr/h    and with 32% of golden on local SQ: sigma_y = 36.23 um, 21% SR capture, 3.6±0.1 hrs lifetime, 2.8 mr/hSo clearly, while the local SQ compensation can get rid of what we assume is local (linear) coupling and the results match what we saw last time (11/24), this does not results in a substantial improvement of dose on the floor, lifetime, or capture efficieny. author: operator_1
subject: LEDA studies
details: In anticipation of future GEMINI ops at low LEDA gap, we checked LEDA effects at small gaps. The goal is to estimate how far topoff goal current would have to be lowered in order to maintain constant current during users.Took 1st baseline with all gaps open except for 5W:LEDA 28 mm: 35% SR capture, 1.1 mA/shot, 4.2±0.1 hrs lifetime, 0.4 mr/h on Portables 1 Gamma 3Took 2nd baseline with user gaps on all but LEDA & 6-2:LEDA 28 mm: 36% SR capture, 1.1 mA/shot, 3.4±0.1 hrs lifetime, 0.4-0.8 mr/hLEDA  8 mm: 29% SR capture, 0.8 mA/shot, 3.3±0.1 hrs lifetime, 1.2-1.6 mr/h...and after LN phase shift...LEDA  8 mm: 35% SR capture, 0.9 mA/shot, 3.5±0.1 hrs lifetime, 1.2-1.6 mr/hLEDA  6.75 mm: 32% SR capture, 0.6 mA/shot, 3.5±0.1 hrs lifetime, 2.0 mr/hLEDA  5.5 mm: 20% SR capture, 0.3 mA/shot, 3.0±0.1 hrs lifetime, 4.4 mr/hThe measurements at 8 mm confirm what we last measured on Nov 11 & 24.And for comparison with all gaps open (incl. 5W)LEDA  5.5 mm: 24% SR capture, 0.3 mA/shot, 3.3±0.1 hrs lifetime, 4.4 mr/hFor gaps below 8 mm an Fl Op was out at GEMINI confirming dose rates with a mater at the rope.Ops at 6.75 mm would be just barely compatible with 500 mA topoff with shots coming in every 15 sec (discounting SB, hence no cam or equalizer) or every 13 sec assuming we maintain SB shots. However, 5.5 mm would call for ~250 mA for topoff to keep up with 0.3 mA every 13 sec assuming absolutely no SB inj.

subject: Trying to improve injection efficiency in nux=16.25 and nuy=9.20 lattice
details: we, i.e. operator_1, operator_2 (and initially operator_3) spent some time trying understand and improve the injection efficiency in the original lowe emittance lattice (nux=16.25, nuy=9.20). We started with RF off and looked at turn by turn data. Looked at sensitivity to booster tune (i.e. mostly vertical emittance at extraction), relative phase, launch (last BTS correctors), BTS trajectory, BTS quads, injection septa, storage ring tunes, storage ring chromaticity, storage ring orbit, static injection bump, pulsed injection bump timing, collimator settings ... While we were able to get the turn-by-turn monitor measured capture efficiency in the optimum to about 90% (as defined by the ratio of the sum signal on turn 10000 to the one after 1 turn), we were unable to achieve ICT derived injection efficiency (i.e. ratio of stirage ring DCCT delta over BTS ICT) above 60%. The sensitivity to all of the parameters seemed reasonable and explainable, but somehow there appears to be a difference to past results. If all of the DCCT and ICT scalings are correct and based on the fact the the turn by turn BPM derived capture efficiency is higher, it appears that some aperture scrapes off some beam during transfer (septum, ...?). Because it did not change when we opened the scrapers, it does not seems to be those. Also, when we added a static injection bump of -1 and -2 mm (thereby reducing the betatron oscillation amplitude of the injected beam) the efficiency did not change. This is an indication that the loss is likely not a dynamic aperture issue, but rather a geometric aperture one (septum?). Will need to think about this more. Some BPM data was saved with operator_3's application for potential post processing.

author: operator_4
subject: LINAC Phase Shifter Analysis and Findings
details: In this session, we focused primarily on the AS2 phase shifter within the LINAC Low-Level RF (LLRF) system, examining both the RF path and the control path from the IRM to the phase shifter. Below is a summary of our findings:1. RF Path AnalysisThe RF signal path consists of the following:Master Oscillator (MO) → Multiplier x6 → LINAC LLRF → PSS Interface Chassis (Coax Switch) → Modulator.Inspection and Tightening of Connections:All connections were thoroughly inspected and tightened, with extra attention to the connections near the klystrons due to the high levels of EMI in this area. In the past, EMI has caused communication issues between the Solenoid Power Supply and the PLC.Input and Output Signal Verification:The RF input to the LBL LLRF chassis is constant and independent of LINAC operation. The power levels at this chassis were verified to be within specifications.For the output signal, we cross-checked the process variables (PVs) for AS2 phase control, readback, and LN coax switch #2. We observed that the anomalies occurred regardless of whether the switch was open or closed, or whether the RF signal was passing to the modulators.Conclusion:The anomaly is not dependent on the RF path, as:No issues were found with the RF cables, adapters, or connectors.The PVs confirmed that the anomalies occur regardless of the state of the coax switch or RF signal passage to the modulators.2. Control Path AnalysisThe control signal path consists of the following:IRM → 3GHz S-Band Control and Interface Chassis → LBL LLRF Chassis.LBL LLRF Chassis Inspection:This chassis contains an instrumentation operational amplifier (gain = 1) that processes the input signal and sends it to the phase shifters.Oscilloscope probes were added to monitor real-time signals from the IRM DAC and the readback signal. No anomalies were found in this section.3GHz S-Band Control and Interface Chassis Inspection:The only passive component in the control signal path, a selector switch, was carefully inspected.We observed that the anomaly could be consistently reproduced by interacting with this switch. Whenever the switch was toggled, it intermittently caused a signal drop to half its normal value, as measured by the oscilloscope.Multimeter testing confirmed the switch was in poor condition. Additionally, the chassis was found to be heavily covered in dust, which was cleaned thoroughly.Conclusion:The anomaly was localized to the selector switch. This switch is used to toggle between two signal sources: the IRM DAC (remote control) and a variable voltage potentiometer (local control) inside the 3GHz S-Band Control and Interface Chassis. The switch’s poor condition caused intermittent signal degradation, introducing the anomaly.3. ResolutionA temporary bypass was implemented to keep the system in remote mode, eliminating the need for the faulty switch. A suitable four-pole double-throw (4PDT) switch could not be sourced immediately.A new power supply was installed in the 3GHz S-Band Control and Interface Chassis to eliminate reliance on the external power source.The permanent replacement of the selector switch is scheduled for the next two-day maintenance shutdown.Final Notes:The issue was conclusively identified as being in the control path, specifically the selector switch in the 3GHz S-Band Control and Interface Chassis. Temporary measures have stabilized the system, and the permanent solution will be implemented during the next maintenance window.Another team member added more information and pictures in these link. Lead: a technical lead.Assitance: a team member, another team member

author: operator_1
subject: Machine setup after installing GEMINI bump
details: At 60 mA, opened gaps, loaded lattice. Corrected orbit to 18/15 microns rms. BPMs to low current mode. Measured ORM. LOCO converged after 3 iterations to 2.917 microns rms of measured (no outliers) with chi^2/DOF = 37.661. ±6% beta beat, significant QDA change needed.Symmetrized and corrected coupling. BPMs back to user mode. OCO to 17/16 microns rms of golden and recorded tunes at 0.153/0.258. Checked all CMs good. Saved golden. Saved new ops files.Cycled. Several SB tolerance alarms. Injected to 61 mA. OCO to 16/15 microns rms of golden. Corrected tunes 0.1588/0.2490 –> 0.160/0.250. All CMs good. Saved new golden lattice.Injected to 500 mA with all FBs, hampered by loss of SHB2. At 500 mA in topoff measured BL31 beam sizes 37.00/52.97 microns rms. Corrected (-0.353 on skew wave) to 37.27 microns rms. Lifetime is 4.3±0.1 hrs, SR capture is 39%. Saved new golden skews (to MML, feedback script, and new skew IOC). Closed 5W and measured 36.89/37.49 microns rms with lifetime 4.2±0.1 hrs. SR capture efficiency is 33%. BSC did not auto-record new offsets so entered them by hand. Adjusted its target V beam size to 34.8 microns. Closed all IDs to user gaps (except for LEDA). Measured 37.34/34.49 microns rms and 3.9±0.1 hrs lifetime. SR capture eff now at 42%. Did not measure chromaticity because 9-1 ID amp faulted.

subject: BL3.1 temperature monitoring vs. beam spot motion

These new PVs should help us correlate and better understand cause and affect.The new PVs  has generated areBL31:CCD:TC0 -> inner temperatureBL31:CCD:TC1 -> bl31 CCD camera temperatureBL31:CCD:TC2 -> experimental area temperatureand they are all archived with the slow policy.I have set up a new striptool I_BL31roi_temps.stp that shows BL3.1 ROI motion (since we have a FB keeping the beam spot centered on the sensor) as well as these new BL TC PVs and the AHU22 CHW valve. This striptool is running on apps3.

author: operator_2
subject: Gas alarms seem to have been set off by Hydrogen
details: Shortly after we gave them the portable gas monitor, users called the CR that their small gas alarm went off again and that the portable monitor was reading CO at ~ 4 ppm. I went out to investigate and saw the CO reading at 3-4 ppm which went down to 0. Oxygen levels were good at 20.9%. Other gases read 0. I recalibrated the device. I checked to see if any BLs are working with CO and saw that BL12.2.1 is. Their hutch was not searched and no users were present. I checked their cabinet and general area with the portable and measured CO at 0ppm. I got another portable 4 gas monitor to verify readings and completed a circle around the experimental floor with two devices reading CO at 0ppm. Left both devices at 8.0.1.4. One at their small yellow gas alarm box and one at their work station. An hour or so later they called again that they had another alarm and CO was around 7-9 ppm on the portables. Note that readings were different between the two handheld devices with one showing around 5 ppm lower. I tried to see where the readings were highest and localized it to BL09.0.2 and BL08.3.2 hutch area where readings were 16-18 ppm. I found out that users in that area are working with helium, oxygen and hydrogen. A user suggested that there might be cross-sensitivity of the CO sensor with hydrogen. I asked the user at BL08.3.2 to direct the hydrogen nozzle toward the 4 gas alarm sensor and the CO sensor went up to 20-30 ppm region.

author: operator_3
subject: LN AS2 Phase FB
details: Related to recent susecpted phase shifter problems, I have prepared a simple little feedback script that will ask the operator for a desired AS2 phase (in V within -10...10) and then attempt to push the AS2 ph SP around until it reaches the point where the AS2 mon matches that desired target phase. The script is on the default GTB path at linacPhaseFB.m and can be run out of any MATLAB console initialized to GTB.Next time the AS2 phase appears to drift, operators can try out this new script. The script should be canceled (in the usual way with ctrl-c) if manual tuning is desired. However, once manual tuning is complete and a desired AS2 phase has been determined, the script can be relaunched and that desired phase supplied as target.The script will detect if AS2 ph shifter is not in ready state and abort if confirmed (to prevent spurious trips due to intermittent CA problems). The script presently has an update rate of about 0.5 Hz and will correct for deviations below 6e-2 by adjusting stepwise at half that. All these parameters can be fine tuned later.Please give me any feedback you have related to problems or change requests.

author: operator_3
subject: Impedance Measurements and TFB Tuning for High Efficiency Lattice
details: I was able to start the impedance measurement process during my shift. The current dependent kick measurements were done for a relative offset of (0,0) in both planes with LEDA open and with LEDA closed. We were ready to start adding the offsets but we ran out of time as we had time with Dymitry (of Dimtel) was beaming in to help set up the filter coefficients and operational parameters for the TFB. We successfully set up filter coefficients in the horizontal and vertical planes for 100 mA and for 500 mA. Both Dymitry and I were satisfied with the symmetry, depth, and cleanness of the notches. The current dependent tune shifts from 100 mA to 500 mA are modest. The present coefficient filter will work well for ramping up the current from 0 to 500 mA top-off mode. The filter coefficients are optimized for 500 mA top-off. If we wanted to optimize them for lower currents (ie for future AP beam study shifts) that can be done with modest changes to the filter coefficients.configuration files were created for the horizontal and vertical plane with filenames highEfficiencyLattice_DB (I should have added a date but I did not).Dymitry signed off to return to his vacation and I have returned to the control. We did not try to modify the tunes (ie using settune) during the optimization. Running gettune at 467 mA with a present TFB configuration gives:0.26750.1935Lifetime is 5.43 hoursNB. All IDs including LEDA were open for the aforementioned work.

author: operator_4
subject: S01 FE Master PLC restored
details: On Friday, during troubleshooting of the S01 FE EPS HMI & PV issue, we realized that the master PLC program was corrupted. Hanjing has reloaded the program and it returned back to normal operation. However, we still are having an issue with the MOXA module that is needed to write, from the subnet, on to the PVs of the phoebus screen. While troubleshooting is ongoing, I do not have an estimated time for this. The only approach for S01 "write" ability, is still via talking to the PLC directly, as of now. We have multiple paths to temporarily change this situations. However, since S01 do not have active users (meaning writing to these PVs would not be an emergency) and to not disrupt accelerator ops, I decided to wait until the next MI day (12/2 & 12/3) to make any changes. Since a complete FE test, to test the PV reading, will interrupt accelerator ops (and also need to write to the PVs to reset them when tripped during test), I did not test all the PVs in S01 FE, but just the PVs that does not impact the accelerator and that do not need resets. Did not see any issues reading those PVs on the phoebus screen (unlike prior to the master PLC fix). With a good amount of certainity, I can say that the S01 FE PVs that we have on the control room screen are accurate representations of their statuses. A final confirmation will be sent out, once I can test these during the MI days.

author: operator_2
subject: Lubricate and Inspect SRRF Cavity 1 and 2 Tuner mechanism
details: Late log entryAs part of our efforts to verify the mechanical functionality of the system, we collaborated with a mechanical technician who supported us during the inspection process.Belt Condition CheckWe first inspected the condition of the belts for both cavities. No signs of wear or damage were observed.Screw Assembly MaintenanceThe screw assembly was thoroughly cleaned of old grease, which was notably hardened, and subsequently re-greased.Tuner Movement TestingUsing the 500 MHz Cavity Phase Tuner Servo Controller Chassis for Cavity 1 and Cavity 2, we conducted movement tests by opening the control loop and manually adjusting the position tuner. The results are as follows:Cavity 1:Initial Test: The tuner mechanism did not jam but exhibited very slow movement during the first operation.Resolution: After lowering and raising the tuner, removing the hardened grease, and applying new grease, the mechanism moved freely across its full range of motion. This process was repeated several times to ensure consistent performance.Cavity 2:Initial Test: The tuner mechanism became stuck at three distinct positions during upward movement and required manual assistance to resume operation. On some occasions, it exhibited sudden jumps.Resolution: As with Cavity 1, we lowered and raised the tuner, removed the hardened grease, and applied new grease. Following these steps, the mechanism operated smoothly and without obstruction. Multiple repetitions of this process confirmed reliable performance.Startup ConfigurationAfter maintenance, both cavities were tuned and adjusted during startup to achieve optimal reverse power levels and proper cavity alignment.ObservationsIn both cases, the presence of hardened grease was identified as the primary issue impeding tuner movement. The cleaning and re-greasing process restored full functionality, enabling smooth operation across the entire range of motion.
category: Accelerator Controls, Accelerator Physics, Electronics Maintenance, Operations, RF

author: operator_1
subject: 2200: Sector 01 EPS HMI issues
details: During start up, operators cannot make up S01 RF permit and contacted me. When I looked at the phoebus displays for the chains, they say that all the PVs that are required for the vac-sum are made up in S01. As the next step, I reached out to EM shop and a technician helped by being the eyes on the PLC in the SR pit - which says that RF permit is not made up (PVs are saying the opposite) and also VVR001 was closed (again, PVs are not agreeing). This confirmed that the PVs are misleading (hence CR also sees wrong PV statuses on their screens). After further discussions with a colleague, had to go in and connected to the PLC directly by bypassing the IOCs and tried to read the reality inside the PLC. Turns out that the IG2C in SR S01 tripped at some point during the MI days and needed a reset to open VVR001. But since the PVs are misleading, this is not shown on the screen and we did not know what is the cause of the chains to not make up. We also cannot write on this HMI now, hence a reset on the HMI would not work.Multiple things happened here1. S01 Master PLC is not funtioning as expected. Since this how we read/write the modicons from the subnet, all PVs in S01 are questionable now. But LabVIEW was connected to the PLC directly via serial, so we did not see these issues previously.2. This Monday, we have converted all FE EPS PCs from windows to LINUX. Which means, we are 100% on Phoebus for FEs and no LabVIEW as a back up anymore. This means the serial connected HMI is not available anymore and the subnet connected PVs are inaccurate as the master PLC is not funtioning properly.Since the only HMI we have right now, aka phoebus, is via the IOC, with no accurate PVs plus cannot write to these PVs, S01 is currently unable to function. More troubleshooting is needed, but as of now, all RF permit chains are made up in S01 and will be frozen in that state. until the PV read/write issue is solvedPlease note that the logic in the PLC has not changed or impacted. It is an HMI & PV issue. So, there is no protection issue in play and hence it is safe to run the machine. Also, during this troubleshooting period, the ultimate source of true status of EPS in S01 is by cheking the PLC LEDs and not the PVs, for now.

author: operator_4
subject: Lowered Low Warning Limits on Modulators for Klystron Ion Pump Currents
details: The WLim (low yellow warning limits) for the Ion Pump currents for the klystrons on both LINAC modulators were lowered from 1.0 nA to 0.1 nA. This is to reduce the occurence of nuisance alarms in the control room on the low end of ion pump currents as they sometimes hover near or jump above and below 1 nA (especially modulator / klystron 1). The low end of Ion Pump currents are less critical than the high end (i.e. low ion pump currents indicate good vacuum as long as there is a separate verification that the ion pump/controller is running). There is also a separate interlock for the Ion Pump voltage (around 5kV) to ensure that the ion pump pumps/controllers are on and running.In addition the EPICs counterpart for these limits were also lowered (actually to 0.01nA) by operator_1 for the same reason.This will be watched over the next operations cycle and adjusted further as needed.
category: Accelerator Controls, Electronics Maintenance, Operations, RF

author: operator_2
subject: Temp control issue SR03 AHU22 vs. observed beam motion
details: We appear to be suffering from a temperature regulation issue with AHU22 which has its air temp sensor at the very d/s end of the SR03 arc.As can be seen in the top plot of the 1st attachment (especially on Nov 9 & 10), the AHU's supply temp (along with its CHW valve) shows rather large swings with ~5-hr period.This then shows up on the BPMs in the SR03 arc in both the V (1st attachment, bottom) as well as the H (2nd attachment). There are only two BPMs here out of the loop (3,5 because broken & 3,7 by design due to energy resolution when EPU 4-1 does ph switching), but the perturbation shows up on at least 3 SR03 arc BPMs and 1 SR04 arc BPM.Meanwhile we've also been observing some large motion of the beam spot on the CCD sensor at the diagnostic BL3.1: the 3rd attachment shows the end of such an oscillation with 5-hr period along with considerble drift in both planes. The oscillation in the V shows an amplitude of about 30 pixels which corresponds to about 230 microns on the sensor or about 12 urad (assuming 20 m to source point). The 12 urad matches actually quite well the roughly 15 microns we see in the V BPM oscillation (1st attachment) keeping in mind that the flanking BPMs at BL3.1 source point are 1.5 m apart: getspos('BPMy',[3 4;3 5]).These oscillations and especially the drift of the beam spot on the CCD leads to spurious beam size variation as we have observed before. The 4th attachment shows at the top the BL3.1 derived H/V beam sizes over the course of the last days. We expect some variation in the V, but the H should be mostly flat due to our very small emittance coupling. Nevertheless, there is strong apparent beam size variation in the H, especially on Nov 10 and 11: about -2.5 microns drift or roughly 6% of the rms beam size. This variation correlates very well with the drift in beam spot centroid on sensor during those two days, see 5th attachment (jump yesterday was due to camera repositioning). The drift observed Nov 10/11 is roughly 100 pixels in the V, which corresponds to about 800 microns at the sensor or ~40 urad from a 20-m source point.https://controls.als.lbl.gov/pvinfo/aa/ui/viewer/archViewer.html?pv=BL31:cam1:MinY_RBVSuch strong variation (~60 microns at source point BPMs) appears significantly larger than any usual beam motion we'd observe in the V plane around that area (see 1st attachment, bottom). This raises the question if there is perhaps a larger issue with climate control in the area of the 3.1 beamline (which could then be driving the strong regulation swings we observe in the tunnel at AHU22).

author: operator_3
subject: 0842: Alarm for Gas Cabinet, BL 9.0.2 (B09_902_B_GAS_ALARM)
details: An alarm event for Gas Cabinet 9.0.2B occurred:  PV: B09_902_B_GAS_ALARM (see sceen shot of PV Info alarm log entries). In my investigation regarding the cause,  I could not find any definative entry in the OLog regarding a history, such as nuisance alarms, related to this alarm.. I then went to the BL to obtain more information. From a confirmation by a beamline scientist of previous information obtained from a BL scientist, I learned that: 1) the gas in the cabinet is not toxic, and therfore the toxic gas monitor there is is not activated, and, 2) the alarm comes on if the door of the cabinet is open for too long, which will cause the airflow sensor to detect too low of airflow exhausting out of the gas cabinet. If the airflow sensor is tripped, the Air Flow Alarm LED on the Face Velocity & Gas Detector at the rear of the cabinet (yellow box) and the beacon that extends vertically from the Face Velocity & Gas Detector box will light up. There is no audible alarm. The alarms connected to the box are turned off by pressing the Alarm Reset Button below the  air flow alarm's LED.Note for the Controls Group: Pressing the reset button did not immediately clear the alarm in the CR. Three (3) hours and nineteen (19) minutes later, the alarm did clear in the CR. This appears to follow a pattern of a long delay to clear the alarm upon a reset after the alarm event.  Conclusion: A gas alarm for Gas Cabinet 9.0.2B is not a major alarm and there is no danger if thia alarm is activated. To clear the alarm, press the alarm reset button described above. The alarm should clear in a few hours.

author: operator_1
subject: BL3.1 CCD position adjusted
details: We've lately been observing quite some beam motion on the BL3.1 CCD. This cannot be directly related to BPM readings at the source point (see below) although we have also seen such ~7-hr period variations on BPMs (albeit at much smaller amplitude) when AHUs in the tunnel hadn't been properly configured. The movement of the beam spot at 3.1 showed a slow oscillatory (period ~ 7 hrs) behavior around a long-term drift that appears to be perhaps related to air temp in the vicinity of the BL. However, over the weekend this drift had become so bad that the ROI bumped up against the lower limit of the CCD sensor. Since we have a ROI position FB that attempts to keep the beam centered (improving fit quality), this started effectively making our ROI far too narrow vertically.In order to fix this, I asked a technician to move the 3.1 CCD which itself sits on stages to better center the beam spot on the CCD. We did this brief operation today. I had paused the ID ML FF to make sure its online retraining (which effectively entails an FB componenent) did not act back on any transients while we moved the spot. The technician moved the beam spot across almost half the 8-mm sensor (at 20 m from source this would amount to 200 urad!) in the V (and about 2/3 of that in the H) plane to get it well centered again. Beam size change before vs. after the move was minimal. Once the spot was nicely centered on the CCD again, we were able to restart the ROI FB on apps1 as well as turn back on the ID ML FF in SRcontrol. Overall duration of ops without ID ML FF was <15 min. All good again.

author: operator_1
subject: Kly HV PS transient
details: Operators received an alarm related to a diff between kly HV VoltDivVd1/2 and the kly HV SP. At first I thought this was perhaps caused by our kly HV FB being a bit slow in adjusting the SP to drifting monitors, but it turns out there was an actual glitch on the HV on both monitors. This was a short, but large transient, about 600 V (see attached).The FB did react to this by adjusting according to its maximum step size (which is not enough to make up for such a large transient on one FB step), but by the next FB steps the transient behavior had subsided and the FB returned to its initial SP.It would be interesting to hear what might have caused such a large transient on both monitors. We don't usually observe that during regular user ops conditions.

author: operator_1
subject: Calibration of EPICS radmon channels
details: We are looking at the difference of the measurements of radiation levels through RPIX to EPICS, and the direct readings into EPICS. The measurements are provided to both systems every 4 seconds, with dose already converted to dose rate in units of mrem/hr. Resolution of this data is only 1mrem/hr.     But some monitors have an internal source that injects a signal to confirm the monitor is working, both acquisition chains should remove this reading by subtracting the measurement when there is no beam.   It is this we are now doing with the direct EPICs data.The RPIX to EPICS data is is available in two channels per monitor , for example:BL8L1:Gamma:DoseRate which is, we are told, the average of the 4 second data over one minute (but see below)andBL8L1:Gamma:DoseRate:Hourly which is the integrated dose over the last hour.The direct EPICS data is available in four channels per monitor, for example :BL8L1:Gamma:DoseRateAvg:4SecondsBL8L1:Gamma:DoseRateAvg:12Seconds   - The average of the last three readings with calibration value subtractedBL8L1:Gamma:DoseRateAvg:1Minute       -  The average of the last fisteen readings with calibration value subtractedBL8L1:Gamma:DoseRateAvg:1Hour          - the average of the last nine hundred readings with calibration value subtractedThe raw data (4Seconds) does not have a calibration factor applied, the others do - at the moment the same factor for all monitors.As can be seen from the attached plot, the resolution of the RPICS data of .3mrem/hr would seem to indicate that this is data averaged over 12 seconds not 1 minute.  As this value goes negative, begs the question, should the direct EPICS system provide also provide negative radiation values when the calibration is subtracted, or zero.  Also the value staying negative over a long period would indicate an issue with the calibration.So should the EPICS calibration aim to provide a result of its own best estimate of actual value from the raw data, or try to match the value provided by RPIX?
category: Operations, Accelerator Controls, Accelerator Physics, Radiation

author: operator_2
subject: Low emittance lattice
details: Drew and I restarted studies on the low-eps lattice. In a dedicated MATLAB console we switched lattice and then ran SRcontrol from there. We started by cycling the ring, We were then able to inject immediately. At 100 mA we corrected the orbit to within 17um rms in both planes and corrected tunes to exactly 0.25/0.20. Saved new golden lattice. 8.5±0.4 hrs lifetime and 53% capture.We loaded the recently saved S/R files for TFBX and Y. Adjusted the tune notch search window and started injecting. While injecting we attempted tuning various knobs in an effort to get beyind 55% capture: SEK, SEN, SR bumps, both BTS final VCMs. But nothing made capture dramatically better, we were only able to make things worse.At ~450 mA we lost stability in all 3 planes. I was able to regain transverse stability by adjusting TFBX shift gain 5->3, but we remained longitudinally unstable. Scrpaed down and regained stability at 278 mA. By turning TFBX/Y on off, we confirmed exactly where betatron tunes were (notch is hard to detect so close to excited parts of the spectrum) and adjusted the SR to get back to proper tunes (dQ=-0.0054/+0.0017). There is considerable tune shift along the injection ramp (feels larger than what we usually see with PSB), but we were able to push tunes back to desired values at higher currents.In this manner we were able to go back to 460 mA. dQ=-0.007/+0.002. At 480 mA we went unstable, clearly first in the longitudinal. No amount of shift gain changes appeared to affect anything. I scraped down to 229 mA to regain stability and we went back to injection. At 417 mA we went unstable. This time I chose to open and close the 3HC loops and we regained stability allowing us to inject all the way to 500 mA. Now in topoff there, we observe no instability. Drew set out to restore design chromaticity however that is proving tricky since the notches are not clear enough at these high currents. TFB/LFB clearly need tune-up for this lattice. Lifetime is 6.1±0.8 hrs at 500 mA (all gaps wide open). Capture hovering around 50%.

author: operator_2
subject: Local compensation for LEDA
details: We inspected local skew and sextupole compensation schemes applied to LEDA at small gaps. With 500 mA topoff and all FBs running (no ML ID FF) we recorded a baseline:LEDA @ 28 mm: 4.6±0.2 hrs, 44±3% capture, BL 31: 40.5±0.2/40.7±3 microns rms.For 10 mm where we last experimented with skew quadrupole compensation, we could not detect any significant V beam size change. We are suffering from an issue with the 3.1 beam size visualization, but the size calculation appears correct. So with closed shutters, we went to a low LEDA gap that gave us appreciable deterioration:LEDA @ 6 mm: 3.6±0.1 hrs, 27±3% capture, BL 31: 40.6±0.2/42.0±3 microns rms.We tried adjusting flanking skews as a pair. Scaled ±100% around SP, but hardly any change on V beam size and the little change we did see was an increase toward even higher values.We tried adjusting just the u/s skew to no avail. Then with just the d/s skew we were finally able to see a beam size reduction. At 20% if golden, 3.1 beam sizes were  40.6±0.2/41.6±3 microns rms. So still by far not enough.But since we were also still battling with 3.1 visualization (and confused about irek's changes not being picked up), we decided to give up skew compensation and instead move over to SHF/SHD compensation geared toward improving lifetime and capture efficiency. We came up with a simple little script (sextScan.m) that ops can run over night to measure capture efficiency and lifetime as a function of scalings of the adjacent SHF and SHD pair. We would like to do this at 6 mm LEDA gap since that creates a situation that is bad enough to require improvement, but no so bad everything immediately falls apart entirely. The script calls the cleaner to make sure we have a clean gap even when we run just MB inj shots without cam or equalizer. Drew will have exact instructions for them. Once they have collected the data, we can refine serach ranges. At that pooint we can also consider moving individual sextupoles rather than SHF/SHD in flanking pairs.

author: operator_1
subject: LEDA gap vs. GEMINI dose & SR performance
details: At 500 mA and with all FBs running we varied LEDA gap with all other IDs at their last user gap settings. GEMINI shutter was opened to observe C filter dose. The following C filter doses (Gamma 3 on Portables 1) along with lifetime and capture efficiency in the SR were recorded:22 mm: 5.1±0.2 hrs, 49±3%, 0.6 mr/h10 mm: 4.8±0.2 hrs, 43±2%, 0.9 mr/h8 mm: 4.5±0.2 hrs, 39±3%, 1.6 mr/h7 mm, 4.1±0.1 hrs, 32±3%, 2.7 mr/h5.5 mm, 3.1±0.1 hrs, 23±6%, 7.9 mr/h4.5 mm, 1.5±0.05%, 12±1%, 26 mr/hThe expert also recorded n dose which reveals how we appear to encounter 2 different regimes as we go to lower gaps. They plan to attach their plot. We note that we today see roughly 30% lower gas pressure at SR01C-IG2 compared to Nov 6/7 (1e-8 vs. 7e-9 today) when we measured 1.2 mr/h at 10 mm. The dose appears to scale well with pressure (at these larger gaps).From a machine point of view, we believe we can tolerate 8 mm. Rad physics concludes that dose at GEMINI remains tolerable down to 8 mm. LEDA is cleared to run down to 8 mm. ID gap watchdog has been adjusted and restarted.

subject: LFB instability
details: As we got to 489mA while filling we got an IGPF:LFB:SRAM:MAXRMSVAL alarm and saw that LFB went unstable.We scraped to 400 which was enough to regain stability. author: operator_2
subject: BRRF Cavity Cell Power Low
details: Following the observations to verify the mechanical part of the system, we worked with a mechanical technician who assisted us with the inspection.First, we checked the condition of the belt, which showed no signs of wear or damage. Next, we cleaned the entire screw assembly of old grease and proceeded to re-grease it. Finally, we tested movement of the tuner using the 500 MHz Cavity Phase Tuner Servo Controller Chassis, opening the loop and moving the position tuner from there.Results: Initially, it got stuck again at the position where the meter showed 4V when the tuner moved up. However, this changed after we lowered and then raised it again. After the second attempt and once the entire screw was greased, the mechanism moved freely across its entire range. We repeated this process several times.During startup, we retuned the cavity cell to achieve the lowest possible reverse power and proper cavity tuning.
category: Accelerator Physics, Electronics Maintenance, Operations, RF

author: operator_3
subject: LINAC Phase shifter
details: In this session, we focused primarily on the PVs that control the shifters, as well as the readback signals we receive in return. Here’s what we observed:The control and monitoring signals travel from the IOC chassis to the 3GHz S-Band Control and Interface Chassis 23W241 located in racks LI18 and LI21, with LI18 controlling the Master Phase and LI21 managing the AS2 phase. From these two chassis, the signals are sent to the LBL LLRF Distribution Chassis Phase Control Chassis to control both phases.In the 3GHz S-Band Control and Interface Chassis 23W241, both the control and readback signals are passive and do not require buffering within this chassis.The control signal is routed through two separate channels in the LBL LLRF Distribution Chassis, each consisting of two op-amps in series. The output from these buffers is split into two signals: one is sent to the RF shifters, while the other functions as a readback signal.In this round of troubleshooting, we focused on the power supply, as the issue showed a thermal constant. We checked the stability of the +/- 15V power supply and observed some instability in the +15V rail.We replaced this power supply with an external one and noted a significant improvement in the readback signals' behavior. After a full day of operation, we observed a substantial improvement in both the Master Phase and AS2 Phase, with no further signs of instability in AS2 Phase. However, the Master Phase signal exhibited a pattern similar to what was observed on October 20.We also observed that changing the power supply affected the output signal amplitude in this chassis. In this chassis, there are also two RF amplifiers that were connected to the positive supply. This change impacted the input signal of the modulators as well as their output, which is currently slightly lower than normal but still has good injection. Modulator 1 Power FWR: 101.87 dBm, REV: 86.63 dBm. Modulator 2 Power FWR: 101.87 dBm, REV: 84.34 dBm.Additional troubleshooting is needed to identify the root cause of the voltage drop in the readback signal.

author: operator_4
subject: HSD troubleshooting
details: The BR KI, BR SEN and SEK signals are monitored by BR2:HSD3 (SN#003),  in rack B0217. The unit was unresponsive on the network and the hardware appeared dead on inspection. I verified the power is present and the fuse is good, confirming what the EMs already observed.  and I configured a spare unit (SN#013) with the same IP address and replaced the failed unit with the spare and full operation of the unit was restored.LN:HSD2 (SN#008) in rack LI1223 that monitors the LN Mods was also showing some system monitor PVs disconnected on the engineering screen. On further investigation, the unit reported an internal IIC bus communication error. The FPGA was rebooted and the unit is now restored to full operation. This is a known issue with LBL software on RFSoC platforms that happens infrequently, and will be investigated offline.

author: operator_2
subject: LEDA local compensation studies
details: Went into topoff at 500 mA with only 5W closed. All FBs running.With LEDA at 28 mm we measure as baseline: 51.5±0.7% capture (avg over 4 shots), 4.63±0.16 hrs lifetime, BL3.1 sigmas 42.85±0.22 / 42.94±0.30 microns, 0.01 mr/h at C filter (portables 1, gamma 3).LEDa at 10 mm: 46.9±3.8%, 4.20±0.13 hrs, 42.79±0.22 / 43.73±0.30 microns, 0.01 –> 1.2 mr/h after shutter opened.First raised and the dropped both adjacent SQSHFs in steps to 80% in order to restore 3.1 V beam size (with local SQ compensation measured 42.96 microns): 48.3±4.4%, 4.58±0.16 hrs, 1.2 mr/h.The GEMINI shutter apparently cannot be reliably kept open so while troubleshooting there progresses, I'll interrupt these local compensation studies and instead let Thorsten start TxT studies.Once Thorsten is done with TxT and shutter gets fixed, I plan to resume compensation studies. First step will be establishing if we can find an adequate SQ compensation for 5.5 mm. Next step will be to investigate if local SHF/SHD sextupole compensation can affect dose at C filter (assuming we have already managed to restore capture eff and lifetime).

details: After the Top-off test I turned on the big magnet PSs and ramped them up. Cycled the lattice with no issues and filled but lost the beam three times. SRRF tripped but no obvious reason. Notably each time the trip happened the LLRF Phase went bad so I had to run LLRF phase fix in matlab. Orbit correction and feedback was working and LFB/TFB seemed normal. Before the trip the LLRF seemed stable. Looked like the beam was just scraping and rf tripping. I checked magnet values and saw that SR control noted when I loaded the lattice that Bend (1,1) setpoint and monitor doesn not appear to be changing. (It also noted that for the known issue with SR05 shd2) We never lost communication with Bend (1,1) however. I tried to put in a setpoint for Bend (1,1) manually and the monitor value moved correctly. I cycled again and I also restarted the BPM control matlab since I didn't see its matlab window only the application. After this I was able to store beam to 500 mA.

subject: Startup issues found and solved so far.
