author: operator_2
subject: LTB BS and B1 - Power On Issues
details: This startup we again had issues turning on LTB BS and B1 power supplies. The issue is due to the boolean controls channels from IRM 23 for power supply ON/OFF being in the external interlock chain for the new TDK power supplies. The current fix is to open the IRM Engineering Panel, open the IRM 23 details screen and turn on the BC20 and BC21 PVs.LTB_____BS_____BC20LTB_____B1_____BC21I suggest we revisit this issue and determine the best path forward. My suggestion is to remove these singals from the interlock chain. I think the current behavior of the TDK power supplies also covers the software seal functionalty but that should be confirmed. When the external interlock was missing from these power supplies tonight it appeared that the entire remote control interface does not work. EDM panels show white for the PVs and I assume the On Control PV would not function. ping might not even work in this state but we should check that next shutdown.

author: operator_2
subject: Secured from EC 02-79 RSS Top-Off Testing due to fault in SBI Chassis SE082
details: Secured from Top-Off testing due to the return of the fault in the SBI Cabinet SE0823 +15V. During Step 5.7 [4][e] the +15V did notreturn when the S080817-CB12 turned back on. We into the box and checked to see if the new LED socket leads were touching and the werenot. Measured +15V Terminal on PS at 1.8V. Disconnected J14 from the compartor board which removes the front test points and LEDs from the circuit.and still measured ~1.8V from PS1 +15V. We disconnected J1 and voltage at PS1 went back to the nominal +15V. We deenergized the boxand measured resistance from the J1 +15V connection to ground with the LED and front test points still removed since J14 remained disconnected.It was 153 ohms. We measured that same path on the spare board of unknown status and fround that it read 66 kohms. Altogether this would indicate the problem remains and is located on the Beam Current Interlock Chassis Comparator Window INTRL Board (23W754).

author: operator_2
subject: Top Off Testing
details: When we arrived for our shift, we took over 5.3 LMI Ch. A & B Test System Time Response.  Dayshift informed us that SR QFA and SR SD failed the time response and needed to be retested.  During our shift we were able to pass the SR SD time response test.  We then begin testing the SR QFA LMI Chain A and B time response test.  We could not get the power supply to pass test.  Following the procedure, we investigated the DV offset values with the DVM's.  Making small adjustments while observing the voltage values and its limits.  We then retested the time response for Chain interlocks.  We could not get SR QFA to pass the time response test.  The failed results were varied in time response values and changing the DV offset did not seem to have a linear output failure (example is seeming to find a good DV offset value the time response value seemed to get better towards the required time response value, however, upon retesting the exact same values in the same manner would yield us a large changes in the time response).  We were observing the large time range changes around 2mS to greater than 9.8mS.  DV offset values were returned to its Appendix [2] SR QFA parameter values.
category: Electronics Maintenance, Operations, Top Off RSS

author: operator_1
subject: SE0823 Beam Current Interlock Chassis Comparator Window INTRL Board Fault
details: While excuting the procedure to replace PS1 in SE0823 we disconnected the J1 connector from the Comparator Window INTRL Board, we decided to pause andre-energize the chassis and measure the +15V. We stopped since the failure had occured before in June of 2023 and the replacement of PS1 didn't fix the problem.Only swapping around the front LED's seemed to fix the problem and this doesn't make sense from a circuit standpoint so we wanted to investigate if the board and not PS1 was the problem. While J1 was disconnected PS1 +15V measure normally and no longer at +1.8V. We deenergized the chassis again and measured the resistancefrom +/-15V connections to ground. +15V to ground: 150 ohms and -15V to ground was 4.5 Mohms. This clearly indicates a problem with the board.We contacted a technical expert and he advised that if it is indeed the board that has failled he would like us to stop Top-Off testing for the evening and resume in the morningfor board replacemant and retest. We currently cannont find a ready spare board in the Top-Off locker nor in MAXIMO. There is a board that has a tag that says "Status Unknown".

subject: End of Shift Testing Status
details: RSSWA-24-037 was activated to replace the power supply in the Beam Current Interlock Chassis. Even if a spare can be located, a swap would not happen until tomorrow morning meaning testing will likely pause here for the night.

author: operator_2
subject: SR10U vacuum
details: SR10U Ion Gauge has (and perhaps always has had) a lot of noise. We read its values two ways - slow over GPIB (SR10U___IG1____AM06) and fast using Analoge reading into an IRM (SR10U___IG1____AM00)So at any one instant these two values usually do not match due to this noiseAssuming nothing can be done about this noise at the hardware level, I would like to compare these signals with a software low pass filter instaled (SMOO field) . This shoudl allow me to check the values at least agree.But this will slow the response time of these signals - should not be an issue for the IRM reading which updates very fast anyway, but will be more obvious for the GPIB signal which is slow.If no-one objects, I will start this test at 11:00

author: operator_1
subject: archiver appliance (arch05) retrieval process was not working
details: Some personnel reported that the retrieval of archived data was no longer working. The archiver engine and mgmt processes still seemed to be working okay. systemctl status epicsarchiverap also reported this error which is odd since the archiver install/config hasn't changed for a long time: Warning: The unit file, source configuration file or drop-ins of epicsarchiverap.service changed on disk. Run 'systemctl daemon-reload' to reload units. I stopped the archiver at 11:19, did a daemon-reload, and restarted it. Things look normal again but there is a 3 minute loss of archived data as seen below: https://controls.als.lbl.gov/pvinfo/aa/ui/viewer/archViewer.html?pv=SR:DCCT&from=2024-10-30T18:17:32.430Z&to=2024-10-30T18:23:34.476Z

author: operator_2
subject: SEN adjustments for good SR capture despite bad vac lifetime
details: On arrival this morning I wasn't satisifed with SR capture efficiency in the low 30s (shots into SR around 1.0 mA) in spite of LEDA parked. Raised SEN by 5 units to 1749 and immediately capture efficiency increased to 44% with shots now in excess of 1.4 mA. Decided to relaunch SEN feedback which is now outputting to a small console at the bottom right of apps3. In spite of the presently low lifetime (~4.1 hrs) these strong shots give us topoff intervals around 40 sec. Leaks? SR01C-IG2 and SR06U-IG1/2 all low 8s now vs. low 9s a year ago, in the case of SR06U, note the slow but steady trend upward over many months) https://controls.als.lbl.gov/pvinfo/aa/ui/viewer/archViewer.html?pv=SR01C___IG2____AM00 https://controls.als.lbl.gov/pvinfo/aa/ui/viewer/archViewer.html?pv=SR06U___IG1____AM00 https://controls.als.lbl.gov/pvinfo/aa/ui/viewer/archViewer.html?pv=SR06U___IG2____AM00

author: operator_4
subject: Low-emittance optics studies
details: Our goal is to try to re-establish the old low-emittance optics on the modern day ALS storage ring, ideally in order to regain near-100% capture efficiency in the SR.We start in PSB mode at 100 mA with a well corrected orbit and record an ORM in the usual manner with BPMs set to low attenuation. Brought up a fresh MATLAB instance and switched to Low Emittance mode. We then performed a LOCO fit to the ...3sb_disp_+nux16_124bpms lattice. No problems, beta beat ~6% in both planes. Symmetrize (to .25/.20) and correct coupling. Nothing odd, see attached changes. BPMs back to regular mode. Corrected orbit, no CMs too far off. We still have 20 mA in the SR. Saved new operational files (ORM, disp, BPM noise) and saved golden lattice (first time since 2013!). Capture eff before any optimization is 63%.Next step will be to get tunes so we can correct them and then also measure (and correct) chromaticity. TFB needs some work for this first: shift TFB filter frequencies to regain MB stability (we are borderline X unstable) and then the spectral ranges to enable tune measurement via notch detection need to be adjusted (to around ~381/305 kHz). Once tune measurement has been re-established we can correct lattice tunes and save the golden again. Then measure chromaticity and correct. Then save golden again. Each lattice save should be acompanied by an orbit check and if necessaary OCO (setorbitgui with ToF is set up on apps3 for that). Finally, we can test a 'manual' SOFB out of that GUI. At that point we can start studying injection optimization and LEDA-beam interplay at this new optics. Drew and Thorsten will continue working on this list..

author: operator_1
subject: SR02S bumps for LEDA mapping
details: Derived bumps through SR02S (using BPMs 1,10 and 2,1) for future LEDA field mapping studies. Started at 500 mA and later performed the rest at just 100 mA (after beam trip). All bumped orbit readings saved in the usual if-0 loop to setoperationalmode.m at the top of our previous list (lines 2356-2547), with comments indicating their intended purpose.Performed V bumps (using -2 -1 +1 +2) up to ±1 mm in 0.5-mm steps. Performed H bumps (using -3 -1 +1 +3 because HCM 2,2 doesn't have enough swing) up to ±3 mm in 1-mm steps.Cross-checked results using an uncompiled SRcontrol with the -1 mm H bump. All good.

author: operator_4
subject: LEDA beam response vs. JH 1,4 scrapers
details: Started adjusting JH 1,4 scrapers. Top scraper was not responsive and did not want to home. Went out to S021820 and hit reset on the chassis. Was able to home 1,4b and 2,6t, but not 1,4t. So instead, this time power cycled the chassis. That then allowed me to home all three scrapers and move them again.Took a baseline. 5W open, orbit corrected and feedbacks running. With JH 1,4 at golden measure 57% SR capture eff and 4.33+0.14 hrs lifetime. Opened JH 1,4 t/b to 3 mm both to ensure they are outside of the limiting apertures the injected beam sees and measured again. Picked up 40 microns of V orbit in SR01C (after OCO/OFBs). Repeated measurements, but no changes observed: 4.41±0.15 hrs and 57%.Closed 5W with all FBs running and repeated: 4.14±0.13 hrs and 54%. LEDA was still at 28 mm up to this point. Carbon filter dose 0.02 mr/h (Gamma 3, Portables 1). Shutter opened and dose 1.2 mr/h max.Closed LEDA to 14 mm. All FBs still running (except for ML ID FF). 3.99±0.12 hrs, 52%, 1.2 mr/h, modest increase of BL3.1 V beam size (~ +0.5 microns).Closed LEDA to 10 mm. 3.93±0.12 hrs, 51%, 1.6 mr/h, very modest increase of BL3.1 V beam size (~ +0.2 microns).Closed LEDA to 5.5 mm. 2.28±0.04 hrs, 20%, 12.0 mr/h, 4 microns BL3.1 V beam size growth.Closed LEDA to 4.5 mm. 1.21±0.03 hrs, 4%, 38.0 mr/h at 475 mA, another 8 microns BL3.1 V beam size growth, beam twist now visibly increasingJH 1,4 scrapers do not appear to be directly involved in our LEDA issues nor significantly affecting dose observed on floor. Put back LEDA LLIM to 14 mm and relaunched ID gaps watchdog. JH scrapers all back to golden.

author: operator_2
subject: BRRF Cavity Cell Power Low
details: Late Log Entry.After being informed of an issue with the power in the BRRF cavity cell, my main focus was directed toward tuning the cavity.I called EM to do a quick system check. During a video call, I noticed that the BRRF HPA showed no issues, but the reverse power was high, indicating that the cavity was out of tune. I suspected that the loop controlling the tuner movement might be malfunctioning. This could be due to mechanical components, such as the bell and screw, or electronic components, such as the linear potentiometer, control loop, RF cables, or driver.I decided it would be best to troubleshoot the issue in person. Upon arrival, we first checked the connection in the 500 MHz Cavity Phase Tuner Servo Controller Chassis to see if there were any disconnection issues. We found no instabilities in the closed loop, meaning the cables were not the problem. Additionally, the tuner position meter showed us that the tuner was very close to the desired point, further confirming that the cables were in good condition.Next, we focused on the tuner position loop, which controls the stepper motor and adjusts the tuning. Usually, when this issue occurs, it’s because the tuner is not moving. To verify this subsystem, we opened the loop in the chassis, disconnected the Twinax cable for the inhibit signal, and moved the tuner position potentiometer to see if there was any response. Initially, the response was slow, and it seemed a bit stuck, but afterward, the tuner began moving properly up and down. I moved the tuner several times to verify it was functioning correctly.Finally, we retuned the cavity cell to achieve the lowest possible reverse power and proper cavity tuning.Observations: The mechanical part of the system, specifically the bell and screw, should be thoroughly checked during the next two-day shutdown.Lead: A. JuradoAssistance: W. Fung, and P Yuzon

subject: Shift Tuning Summary (made it to 500 mA finally)
details: Injections became weak and erratic when we reached ~470 mA around 6pm or so. BR beam was weak and inconsistent. LTB TV 3 did not work and tuning was tricky. I was able to turn it around briefly by adjusting Linac Phases blind. But things would drift again. Inj efficiency also dropped and I turned off the feedback that was started by the day shift. operator_1 fixed the LTB TV3 from home but I was not able to turn things around right away. I had to retune everything, from the Linac through BTS, to make a difference/increase SR current above ~ 460 mA when SR lifetime is ~ 2 hrs (the high was ~ 470 mA around 6 pm earlier). BR beam is strong and consistent now, mostly around ~ 1.5 nC and above. SR inj efficiency is well above 55% for most shots and injections are almost all above ~ 1 mA. Even the single bunch shots are around 0.3 mA ( ~ 50% effciency). I left the single bunch goal current at ~4.8 mA  because 0.3 shots are getting it above 5 mA anyway. We need to set it to 5 again if single bunch shots became weak. We reached 500 mA a few mins ago. SR01 vac is good, staying below than the earlier high because we had time to scrub when SR current was hovering around ~ 460 mA for a few hrs, while tuning.

author: operator_3
subject: Beam current limited by vacuum recovery.
details: During the maintenance period, we were forced to replace an in-vacuum component in the storage ring due to excessive heating and radiation production. This was the "flexband" between the SR01 arc and SR02 straight, a component that allows for thermal expansion and contraction, mechanical alignment of neighboring structures, and provides an electrically smooth path for the electron beam.Unfortunately the vacuum recovery has not been as quick as expected, so when we open shutters at 8am today we expect the beam current to be somewhat low. Exactly what level we can get to depends on scrubbing between now and 8am. Our plan is to open shutters with whatever current we can reach, then slowly increase the current using topoff injection as the day goes on and the vacuum allows. Conditions other than current will be normal user beam: normal beam orbit control, insertion device control, etc.Please direct any questions to the Control Room. A level-1 email should follow soon to inform the rest of the scientific community.Thanks for your patience and understanding.

author: operator_3
subject: Trobleshooting BR Beam issue
details: We did not even have 1st turn in the BR even after the BR Bump2 is working. BRRF power is good and eveything seems to be on. I checked the BR gate valves earlier, all BR gate valves are shown green on BR Gate Valves section on the Beam Protect page. But two of the BR gate valves were shown purple on the ALL Gate Valves page. I toggled them but nothing changed. Since they were ok on the main beam protect page, I thought maybe it was just a read back issue on this other page. When troubleshooting with operator_1 via text, I checked the beam protect page again and saw that this time two BR gate valves were red and also on the All Gate Valves page (no longer purple). I was able to opened them this time and we were able to circulate beam in the BR. The discrepancy between these gate valves pages made it difficult to detect this problem right away. (operator_2 was working with some BR IRMs. The gate valves that were in weird state or got closed were BR3 VVR1 and VVR2.)

author: operator_1
subject: GTL SOL 3 TCR Power Supply
details: During turnover I was informed that GTL SOL 3 would not turn ON.  We headed down to the Linac area to investigate the problem.  We decided to measure the input voltage to the power supply.  We did not measure any voltage on the rear of the power supply.  The wires had labels indicating it was from LI02 ALS Focus System Control Chassis 23W1215.  We decided to switch from remote to local for GTL SOL 3.  We were able to turn the power supply ON in local mode.  However, we could not output any current using the front panel dials on the power supply.  We placed a clamp meter on the output and verified no current output.  CR noticed a seal on the IRM page (see ops Olog entry).  Disconnecting PG1 and PG2 on the rear of the power supply did nothing either.  I then headed to the CR to observe the IRM page to obtain more information.  Once in the CR, OIC indicated what they observed on the IRM page and Power Supply control panel.  I then had operator_1 power cycle the power supply OFF and switch the Local/Remote to Remote.  Then requested to have operator_1 power the unit back ON.  We then observed a green ready in the CR.  I then asked OIC to command the unit ON.  The PS turned ON and was verified ON at the power supply.  We then slowly restored the output back to nominal value.  Seems to be okay at this time.

author: operator_2
subject: GTL SOL3 appears to be working now
details: The solenoid wasn't ready and was off. The IRM page displayed a seal for the output and couldn't be reset. EMs power cycled in remote which didn't help. Then power cycled in local twice. Once it was back in remote we had a ready green light and was able to turn it on from the Control Room. Ramped it up slowly to setpoint.Before the solenoid was fixed we were able to keep around 380 mA and even climb a little by temporarily retuning the Linac and LTB. After the solenoid was at setpoint we restored a previous GTB lattice and are now climbing fast in top-off mode to 500 mA.

author: operator_3
subject: LEDA studies
details: At 500 mA topoff with only 5W closed and all FBs running, I turned off tune FB and scanned LEDA gap from 28 mm to 5.5 mm (shutter closed) to record tune shift. Tune shift in both planes was slightly larger than last measured in Mar 2023 (see attached). However, this difference is still small compared to the much larger increase we observed between Sep 2020 and Oct 2021 (see plots attached to OLOG entry from Mar 30, 2022)Once this scan was complete, I turned tune FB back on and we opened the shutter so could take data from GEMINI diagnostics like we had done earlier in the day but now at 5.5 mm gap instead of 14 mm. Ops started by measuring fields at GEMINI both in topoff and decay. Note that even in topoff we were dropping current quickly due to only 2 hrs lifetime at 5.5 mm (along with 25% capture, about half of what we now see with LEDA open).Once Ops had completed their surveys we put in the bump across SR02S that centered light on DIAG116. In the V we were able to roughly confirm the desired angular shift, whereas in the H we needed substantially more inboard bump than we had thought in the morning (using DIAG112). However, DIAG116 (light through mono) also allows much better centering than DIAG112 so these revised angles should be used: we require for getting max signal centered on DIAG116 in the V -140 urad (down) and in the H +72 urad (outboard). With this bump left in for just another short while, we asked Ops to run one more survey at GEMINI. They reported seeing the same 11.7 mr/hr as before without the bump, however, by now the current had decayed to 430 mA. So this bump did not lower fields.The bump was again removed so the electron beam is now back to its usual unbumped golden orbit.We opened the gap to 28 mm, restored all FBs, and set the LEDA gap LLIM as well as the watchdog for LEDA back to 14 mm.

author: operator_4
subject: Delayed Entry: Follow-up to ARRF HPAs LCW Flow Tests on 10/04/24
details: Delayed Entry: This entry is providing follow-up information and summary conclusions to the LCW flow testing of the ARRF High Power Amplifiers on 10/04/24. This was to assess any impacts to the normal ALS LCW flows when one or both of the ARRF HPAs were running at their full LCW flows. The LCW valves to each ARRF amplifier were opened all the way (first just HPA01 and then both HPAs) to also account for extra flow due to the Dummy load for each amplifier. However, no downstream components (e.g. circulators, cavities, etc.) for the ARRF chain were in the LCW circuits yet. So only the HPAs and their dummy loads were approximately accounted for. The attachments show the screenshots of the PLCs showing the flows for each HPA (varying between 131.2 to 136.9 LPM or ~34.5 to 36 GPM for each HPA). The HPA# and timestamps are given in the file names.In prep for these tests all the ALS systems were brought to their safe de-energized states so as to protect them from any potentially damaging trips but still drawing approximately normal Operations LCW flows. The SRRF Kates valves were adjusted to be wide open for worst case flows on the SRRF cavities (this is seen as the first step down in the plots from the original OLOG 164842 from 10/04/24). Both SRRF klystrons and all other RF systems were running at their full LCW flows.The results of the flow tests on the HPAs show that pretty much across ALS when both HPAs were running we saw between 1.5 to 2% reductions in flows. However, with only one HPA it was of course approximately half of that. We also again had our RF system Kates valves wide open (worst case condition) and also both SRRF klystrons running (in terms of LCW) and all other RF as well as power supply and magnet systems running at approximately their OPs levels of flows. However, again, electrically all the systems were off in a safe state so as to not risk tripping a system while energized and potentially causing damage (as for example power supplies don't like to get cycled).The CR room staff and ACC physics and other personnel also reviewed the data and it was determined that with two HPAs running we were starting to get uncomfortably close to where interlocks were set to. However, with only one HPA running it was deemed that there was sufficient safe margin and this shouldn't impact Operations. So the plan (as noted) is to conduct the HPA commissioning (SAT) with only one amplifier and its associated LCW load running at a time.We do have a longer term issue as that when the ARRF circulators and cavities and all the magnet and power supply systems come on line there is simply not enough LCW capacity with the current system to support that and still run Dual Klystron mode and APEX. There has been discussion on increasing the pump capacity feeding the overall ALS LCW system but it does not appear that upgrade will be completed in time for the ARRF commissioning before dark time. A couple of alternative temporary mitigations mentioned would be to go to single klystron mode in the SRRF and also turn off APEX. All of that is still under discussion and those mitigations are only required a bit further down the road and not for the HPA commissioning / SAT next week.

author: operator_2
subject: LEDA bump scans
details: In order to figure out misalignment of GEMINI relative to our golden orbit, operator_2 and I ran bump scans through LEDA. At 100 mA topoff with only 5W closed we ran LEDA to its current minimum gap at 14 mm and turned off FBs. Ran bump scans until we had maximized SNR at the center of GEMINI DIAG112. At 500 mA (with all FBs on while injecting) and LEDA at 14 mm we repeated the bump scans. The angles to center on DIAG112 were confirmed at 500 mA. The required angles were determined as -10 urad H (inboard) and -124 urad V (down). With the bump in, ops performed survey.

subject: Machine Setup
details: Opened gaps, loaded lattice. Had ops inject to 62 mA. Corrected orbit to 24/16 microns rms. BPMs to low current mode. Measured ORM. LOCO converged after 3 iterations to 2.895 microns rms of measured (1 outlier removed) with chi^2/DOF = 37.309. ±10% beta beat, significant QDA change needed.Symmetrized and corrected coupling. BPMs back to user mode. OCO to 18/19 microns rms of golden and corrected tunes to 0.162/0.252. Checked all CMs good. Saved golden.Cycled. Injected to 61 mA. OCO to 17/19 microns rms of golden. Corrected tunes 0.145/0.258 –> 0.160/0.250. All CMs good. Saved new golden lattice.Injected to 500 mA with all FBs. At 500 mA in topoff measured BL31 beam sizes 42.9/51.6 microns rms. Corrected (-0.1901 on skew wave) to 43.1 microns rms. Lifetime is 4.8±0.2 hrs, SR capture is 64%. Saved new golden skews (to MML, feedback script, and new skew IOC). Closed 5W and measured 42.6/43.8 microns rms with lifetime 4.5±0.1 hrs. SR capture efficiency is 58%. BSC did not auto-record new offsets so entered them by hand. Adjusted its target V beam size to 41.1 microns. Closed all IDs to user gaps (except for LEDA). Measured 42.4/39.2 microns rms and 4.1±0.1 hrs lifetime. SR capture eff now at 38%. Measured chroma with only 5W closed as 1.270/1.606.

author: operator_2
subject: Matlab Software
details: I recopile the SR Matlab applications this morning to fix a small issue with the SQEPU family.  Please relaunch srcontrol before saving a new Golden lattice, otherwise the EDM screen regeneration won't be correct for the SQEPU family.  Note: SQEPU gets saved but not restored in the lattice file because it's only used for ID feedforward (ie, the golden values are zero). The problem emerged because over the shutdown I converted a number of MML families to use new PV naming -- mostly families that use Caen and TDK power supplies.  For the SQEPU family I missed the fact that if a magnet family is used in ID feedforward the MML Setpoint field can't be the actual power supply setpoint PV.  Instead it's dummy PV that gets summed with the FF setpoint before being sent to the actual power supply PV.  You can get to the actual setpoint using the engineering screen but beware that feedforward will overwrite any changes that you make.

author: operator_2
subject: BBA and new golden orbit across SR02S
details: Since we had once again moved BPM 2,1 due to SR02S work during the SD and since the SR02S orbit had already been fudged due to a misalignment between accelerator and GEMINI, we decided to revisit BPM offsets in that area and record a new golden orbit. Bump studies once we can open the GEMINI shutter will inform S&A as to realigmnment of GEMINI.Performed BBA for BPMs 1,7 (new Y offset 0.2043); 1,9 (new X/Y offset -0.0292/-0.5010); 2,3 (new X/Y offset -0.0288/-0.7666); and 2,4 (new Y offset -0.1347). The new Y offset on 1,9 and 2,3 already indicated low compared to the previous GEMINI bumped golden by ~300 microns which is in line with the V aperture scan we did yesterday showing the beam wants to go low through SR02S by about ~375 microns. We applied these new BPM offsets and also set the golden in these BPMs to these values. Injected 50 mA and performed orb corr to updated goldens (with user attentiations since that is how we otherwise define our user golden) using the usual CM pattern, but with BPMs 1,10 and 2,1 out of the config. This resulted in rms CODs of 17/20 microns. We recorded the resulting orbit for these BPMs (including 2,5 which was part of the previous GEMINI bump) and update the goldens to these values. No significant changes on the CMs. Then we brought BPMs 1,10 and 2,1 back into the config and corrected once more. Orbit is 20/20 microns rms.With this new golden obit we repeated the V aperture scan through SR02S, see attached. Now the beam wants to be ~100 microns low, but since the uncertainty on the recorded lifetime levels and the drop-off is on ther same scale, I'm choosing not to bump the beam anymore at this point and instead consider this our new golden orbit.As soon as GEMINI can open their shutter, we will perform bump studies to ensure that we know by which angles GEMINI components need to be realigned to finmally again be in line with both the accelerator and LEDA.Next step will be a fresh machine setup on this new golden orbit.

author: operator_2
subject: SR03S vacuum recovery
details: Yesterday at around 9:22am operator_1 switched off SR03S-IP4 for us after we had observed many beam trips that seemed to be caused by spikes on either IG1 or IG2 without having found any leaks or other signs of real vacuum trouble in that area. IP4 had been reading high (~1e-7) for a long time, even durin the last user run, regardless of VVR settings or power to cavities or beam current. It had also been observed that the pressure reading changed by a decade when swapping IP4's controller. After IP4 was switched off, IG1 and IG2 immediately became much more calm and showed far fewer noisy spikes and of those that remained were of much lower amnplitude. No other IPs or IGs showed any pressure increase after switching off IP4.IP4 has now been off for almost a day and we have not suffered a single vac trip since in the RF straight despite full cavity power with 500 mA and gaps closed. IG1 and IG2 remain quite calm, see attached.

author: operator_3
subject: BR KE4 troubles
details: Total Summary of issues and fixes for Booster Extraction Kicker 4: 10/08/24 (Tues) We found 500k burnt resistor stack and other cracked resistors inside of Pulse Forming Termination Chassis (23w2993).10/10/24 (Thur) We replaced the kicker tube and B-DOT Buffer / Integrator & C Temp chassis (23W3463). This fixed the issueIn depth: On Tuesday (10/08), we looked in the Pulse Forming Termination Chassis and found the 500K resistor stack burnt and one of the resistors for the diode board cracked. This did not fix the issue (needed to happen anyways). We also changed out the diode board (the previous board was tested good after removing). At this time we tried testing for shorts with the KE4 Filament and Reservoir off and found little.On Thursday (10/10), we did more tests with a test power supply. With the KE4 Filament and Reservoir off (cold thyratron tube), we found nothing. Eventually, we decided to test it again, but with the KE4 Filament and Reservoir on (hot thyratron tube). This did show a short circuit this time.We also saw the KE2 and KE4 had their bias voltages mixed up (the 2 metal rings behind the metal face). The HV box should be going to bias 2, the back ring. The BNC barrel should be going to bias 1, the middle ring. We swapped them to what they should be.Switching the bias did not fix the issue, so we swapped out the KE4 tube and this fixed the short circuit. The KE4 Glassman Power supply was able to come up to voltage.However, triggering was acting weird, so we replaced the B-DOT Buffer / Integrator & C Temp chassis (23W3463). This fixed the issue and everything is working.We then retimed the kickersThyratron Tube IN: J050     OUT: J049
category: Accelerator Physics, Electronics Maintenance, Operations, Power Supplies

author: operator_1
subject: Vertical aperture scan LEDA straight
details: In 16-bunch mode we did a V aperture scan through the LEDA straight using the (as of now still uncalibrated) BPMs 1,10 and 2,1. Beam low first, then beam high. Results attached. This aperture scan shows the same picture we've seen in the past where the beam wants to be low by ~375 microns. This is consistent with past scans which have always had us lower the beam through the straight by 0.2-0.3 mm.The plan is now to confirm with BBA the offsets on adjacent BPMs (1,8 is out of MML, 2,2 is the MBFB pickup) and then set new goldens by using full ToF orbit correction toward these offsets without 1,10 and 2,1 in the mix. Then, we will lower the beam by adding a static -300 micron V offset to these new values and call that the new goldens. We will then do a fresh setup to this new golden orbit and finally repeat this V aperture scan to confirm. From lowering the beam through the straight we can expect a ~ 15% increase in Touschek lifetime which is welcome considering we are presently still a bit on the low side (~ 4.4 hrs with all gaps but LEDA closed).That effort will be followed by bumping through LEDA again once GEMINI is qualified to take light (~ Mon/Tue) so as to determine angles for GEMINI realignment as previously discussed with GEMINI and S&A team. This should result in a situation where the electron beam is reasonably well aligned through the straight (i.e. both to neighboring quads thus preserving beam quality as well as to vac enclosure), runs centered through LEDA magnetics, and still maximizes flux by the time light reaches the GEMINI end station.

author: operator_1
subject: LATE ENTRY: Change to SRRF Cav1 vacuum trip levels yesterday.
details: While troubleshooting the RF vacuum trips yesterday, we found that SRRF Cavity 1 had its trip levels misconfigured.Both cavities have a "SP1" trip level that is the real interlock and will trip the RF and close gate valves.Both cavities have a "SP2" trip level that is only connected to the controls system to give us an alarm (but I don't know what PV that connects to).For Cavity 1, SP1 and SP2 were switched, with SP1 at 1e-8 and SP2 at 5e-7, making the cavity much more susceptible to vacuum events. We changed them to match cavity 2.Unfortunately vacuum spikes continue, and though trips seem to be less often, we still had a vacuum trip last night at 500mA.

author: operator_2
subject: Re-enabled slow phase feedback
details: Noticed going from 300 to 400 mA that our SRSF master loop phase appeared a bit low compared to what I think is usual these days. Noticed that somehow no slow phase feedback had been running and consequently we had incurred about 35 counts of servo delta by the time we reached 400 mA. Launched slow phase FB on apps3 and immediately servo delta was minimized while SRRF master loop phase increased a couple deg. All good now. Brief reminder: on apps3 when we run as for users we should always see at least 3 operational MATLAB feedbacks running: SRRF kly HV SP FB, slow phase FB, and IG gaps watchdog. BTS traj FB is optional. All of these MATLAB FBs are equipped with time stamps on their console output that serve a heartbeat to assist monitoring alive/well.

author: operator_3
subject: Update on BR KE troubleshooting.
details: (posting on behalf of a colleague) BR KE4 kicker pulser Glassman charging PS was drawing ~2mADC at ~1kV.  EMs found a series charge resistor array in the chassis in the tunnel which had burned up from too much power - an indication that there was a short to ground after the series charge resistor array.  The diode board to clamp negative voltage reflections at the output cables in the same chassis in the tunnel was dirty, but even though it passed a quick 4kVDC HV test with insignificant leakage current, it was replaced.  The Ross HV relay in the HV distribution chassis in the pit racks and the Ross  HV relay which is in the chassis in the tunnel appeared to be opening correctly.  Disconnecting the charging circuit from the output cables showed the short to ground on the charging side of the circuit.  The charge cable was disconnected at the tunnel end for a test and was not the source of the short to ground.  The decision was made to regroup and let startup activities continue with 3 out of 4 BR extraction kickers.   The KE4 Glassman PS was admin locked out since the cable is still disconnected in the tunnel, but it is not an electrical hazard because the end of the cable is enclosed in an insulator and protected within the grounded chassis.  There are labels in the pit and in the tunnel to communicate the temporary configuration of the system.  The next test will be to only connect the charge cable to the filter capacitor in the chassis in the tunnel and confirm that the capacitor is not the problem...although this would not explain the failed series charging resistor array since it is before the resistor array.  We will review the circuit and resume when it's compatible with startup activities on Wednesday.  Thanks to the EMs and EIs who supported the debugging process.
category: Accelerator Physics, Electronics Maintenance, Operations, Power Supplies

author: operator_4
subject: Hi-Potting
details: Adrian found us a Digitel SPCe, so we were able to use the Hi-Pot mode and attempt to reach a voltage of 10 kV on the following ion pumps: SR03S IP1, SR03S IP2, SR03S IP4, SR03S IP5, SR03S IP6, SR03S IP7 and SR03S IP8.  We were able to reach 10 kV on all but IP1 and IP4.  SR03S IP1 reached about 8 kV and SR03S IP4 reached about 7.5 kV.  The display would read Pump Stopping after at most 2 seconds, regardless of the voltage reached.  Sol asked us to go through this process again (up to three times) to see if there was any more improvement.  We went through the hi-pot process again on the seven ion pumps, trying IP1 and IP4 three times each.  We think we saw slight improvement, but agreed that it wasn't noticeably better with each try.

author: operator_4
subject: BR tuning (with LTB alingment)
details: I did not have an opportunity to tune/stabilize/maximize the BR during the RF bellow testing period. BR beam intensity was changing a lot. The abosolute max was ~ 1.4 nC while lows are like ~ 0.4 nC. There also was shot to shot variations: one shot high but the next was low. BR parameters were well off from our normal range, for example, B offset was 403. Restoring to the normal range, 600 - 650, did not work. QF and QD plots did not align with the golden plots. Simply aligning them did not work. It seems that extensive tuning is required. I was able to tune today in parallel with finishing up EPBI 2 test. I set the BR B to 605, and lowered IFT to 14200 range (from 14300 range). Then, I worked on finding the good QF and QD offsets. I touched up with adjusting all three gain sepoints (it took several iterations). Finally, I fine-tuned the LTB to maximize the BR beam. BR beam max is now above 2.2 nC and there are no more low shots. BR waveforms plots are all aligned.

author: operator_1
subject: Tuning Summary for 2 swing shifts
details: Tuning Summary for Yesteray (I did not have time): we had to raise the EGun Bias to 80 (max) and detune the AS2 to reduce BR beam current after I tuned the LINAC, LTB and BR parameters, to evenly and slowly fill the SR without creating too much heating and radiation. We had to cut the BR beam back quickly and did not even try to maximize it. I was not asked to tune the BTS, for this lattice.At the start of the swing shift today, I saw that the Gun Bias was back to 30 but the BR beam was very poor, around 0.2nC, and we were barely stacking the SR current. I restored the LTB parameters to what I had yersteday, And then, I made Linac phase adjustments. Finally, I touched up the LTB alignments for these new phase values. The BR beam went to ~1.4nC, and I had to raise the bias quickly to 80 to reduce the radiations. Inj efficiency into SR is very poor compared to yesterday. A supervisor asked me to tune the BTS as I would normally do for User Ops (lattice). The normal BTS tuning improved the effciency greatly and hence the radiation levels. The inj effciency is ~ 50%. We are able to fill the ring much more quickly than yesterday. Currently, gun bias is 80, BR DCCT is ~0.4 nC and fill rate is ~0.15mA to 0.25 mA per shot. Rad in the Inj Are (combination of Gamma and Neutron) is ~25 mR/hr and Gamma 3 (portable 2) is below 0.5 mR, at ~100 mA in SR. It was decided to fill to 200 mA.

author: operator_4
subject: Lowered injection bumps - saved lattice
details: Earlier today , during a period of poor injection efficiency, that the apparent lifetime with poor injection was substantially worse and immediately improved when stopping injection (or more appropriately once stopping injection bumps pulsing). One could also see on the turn by turn BPMs that there were steps down in the sum signal, exactly at the time the SR bumps were pulsing.The root cause for this was that the static injection bump of -3.5 mm, that was optimized yesterday to achieve optimum injection efficiency at low current, brought the stored beam too close to the septum, so that the pulse of the SR bumps was scraping some stored beam off at the septum.This also in hindsight explains why all fills so far slowed down, once we got to higher current (since the loss would be proportional to the stored beam current).The recipe to optimize this is: Switch injection on, put a linac paddle in so that no beam is actually injected. Look at how much stored beam is knocked out at each injection. Compare that to the slope of the beam current (i.e. the lifetime) if you stop injection. Now reduce the injection bump until there is no significant amount of beam knockout. This is admittedly a judgement call. Finally verify that injection efficiency is still acceptable. This is where the judgment call comes in since there is a trade-off. A larger injection bump improves the efficiency with which the beam from the booster is captured by also increases the stored beam losses in each shot.I found that to me at about 50 mA, a static injection bump of about 3.0 mm was the optimum. So I implemented that and saved the lattice (both as a tme stamped save and as the 1.9 GeV TopOff production lattice).Afterwards, injection was much improved without changing anything else and 100 mA stored beam was reached (from the starting point of just below 50 mA) within about 15 minutes.

author: operator_4
subject: Directions for scrubbing.
details: The radiation level criteria is to keep the sum of the 1-hr integrated doses of SR02 roof gamma and SR02 roof neutron monitors below 30 mR in one hour.Pause filling as needed to remain below this level as you make your way up to 100mA.Fill to 100mA, refill at 90mA. Once you get to 100mA and start this refilling cycle the rad levels should stay comfortably low and not require pausing during the fills.No orbit correction, try to avoid loading the lattice, but do it if you need to. Cycling should work fine if the need arises.

author: operator_1
subject: RF-bellows test for ALS-U
details: The first test of the startup is the RF bellows test for ALS-U, since the test assembly needs to be removed to switch to the nominal user lattice later during the startup.We followed commissioning plan AL-1664-0401, including radiation hold points. In addition, operators carried out radiation surveys during the test based on a specific radiation survey plan prepared by a physicist.To start, one switches to the HiLo lattice, with large horizontal beta function in the injection (and all odd straights) and a smaller beta function in the rf-bellows test straight (straight 2) and all even straights. This lattice is saved in Matlab as the 1.9 GeV TopOff lattice (the very first mode in the list), since it is similar to that historic lattice, which is not used anymore. We loaded the lattice (production lattice) with srcontrol. Cycling needs to be done manually:srramp(1.522,'LinearByEnergy')srramp(1.89,'LinearByEnergy')Followed by another load of the production lattice.When injecting, we immediately had very high dose rates upstream of LEDA. Turn by turn-monitors showed all beam lost in arc 1. Switched to on-demand injections and tuned up the thick and thin septum based on turn-by-turn data. Afterwards we scanned the tunes around by ~0.05 in both x and y to get to stored beam. Corrected the orbit and increased injection bump from -2.0 to -3.5 mm. Saved the lattice (as a timestamped save, not the procuction lattice). With this, we got injection efficiencies in the 10-20% range, which is within the expected range given the very tight aperture (11 mm) of the test assembly. At full booster repetition rate and charge, the dose rates on the roof were above the hold point of 30 mrem/h that we need to stay below, so we raised the gun bias to get to an acceptable injection rate with acceptabel dose rates.Overall it took a little over 1 hour to reach our goal of 100 mA. With the rf-bellows in its noninal centered position, we observed fairly minimal heating even at 100 mA (<0.5 degree C). To allow offline analysis, we save the BCM trace to the HiLo lattice data directory.After dumping the beam, we went into controlled access mode and offset the RF bellows assembly nominally by ~1mm vertically (the middle part between the SR and AR prototype bellows). At first we got no injection but realized that BTS B1 and B2 had been restored to the golden values, not the values from earlier today. After restoring those, injection immediately resumed. We again managed the dose rate and this time tried to improve injection efficiency a bit, but generally the situation stayed similar (with small improvements in the injection efficiency). Thermal drifts did need some optimization (septa). In this condition we saw a bit more heating on the bellows (~3 degree C at 77 mA).

author: operator_1
subject: Reconfigure water flow for old booster bend power supply+tested interlock
details: We reduced the flow to the new booster bend power supply to 1 GPM for each of the two halves and fully opened flow channel to old power supply. Flow to old supply if the new supply has no flow is 12.5 GPM, total flow with the old supply and the throttled new ones is 12.4+1+1 GPM = 14.4 GPM. So the old supply gets virtually the same flow as it always had with this minimal bypass flow through the new one.Afterwards we tested the water flow interlocks successfully. The old supply trips on waterflow if one closes its flow channel. Old power supply trips on magnet flow, if one raises the sector trip point on the PLC above the actual flow.so waterflow configuration is now ready for the operation of the old power supplies and iwater interlocks passed their functional test. Afterwards we restored the sector trip point to its previous value.

author: operator_2
subject: Inverpower Power Supplies
details: Notified by CR that SR10 HCM3 and SR5 VCM3 cannot be reset in the control room. I went to check the possible issues with the inverpower PS and found that the circuit breaker for SR10 HCM3 was de-energized. Noticed all the front LED indicators for SR10 HCM3 turned on (except ON LED) after I energized the circuit breaker.When I arrived at SR5 VCM3 location, I noticed that all the front LEDs of the power supply were off as well but with circuit breaker in the tripped position (middle). Thinking that the circuit breaker might have tripped off during the shutdown, I tried to push it down first before attempting to switch it on. Unfortunately, the power supply was still not energized even after switching the circuit breaker on. I also noticed that the circuit breaker did not look to be all the way up, it was back in the middle just like how I first saw it. I tried to switch the breaker again but this time I noticed that as soon as I let go of the breaker, it slid back to the middle. Following electrical safety precautions, I went to check for voltages on the power cord and found that no voltage was present even with the circuit breaker switched to on. It seems like the circuit breaker would not stay engaged. Notifed CR of a possible circuit breaker problem.

author: operator_2
subject: LTB BS, B1, B2
details: After talking with technician in the EM shop, it appears to me that the new TDK power supplies in the LTB appear to have some confusing boolean controls and interlocking.  The BC20 and BC21 Boolean controls in IRM23 don't appear to be active IRM channels but they clearly are.BC20 -> appears to be connected to the new TDK interlock for BSBC21 -> appears to be connected to the new TDK interlock for B1These used to the on/off control for the old power supply.  Since that power has been moved to an Ethernet based TDK power supply, it make sense that the PVs would disappear (or ideally they would be aliased to the new PVs).  But they are still involved in the system.  I could have guessed this was done to maintain the software seal for turning the power supplies on, but IRM 23 doesn't have any software seals.  The old power mostly likely did.  It's better to put the software seal in with the EPICS control of the new TDK so that's expected, but I don't know why BC20 and BC21 affect the operation of the TDK.  If it's to maintain the interlock (3 opto's -> control power (BM00), interlock (BM01), and safety chain (BM02)), that would not to good.  For one it would put the IRM in the interlock chain which isn't allowed and without with software seal active it's actually not doing anything!!!  Ie, BC20 and BC21 can be manually turned on and I don't see what would turn them off besides manually turning them off.In any case, after a brief conversation with technician it appears the IRM in somehow involved in the interlock functionality of the BS and B1 power supplies.  If true, this would be a departure from how we have handled interlocking in the past.  It's not my area, but I believe it should be reviewed.   The table below is from the old ILC mysql database. author: operator_3
subject: Booster Kicker Extraction
details: We started to test the Booster Extraction Kicker system.  Prior to the summer shutdown the BR KE system encountered issues (check olog date 09/06/2024 for more info).  After speaking with the OIC, we decided to begin with conditioning the system.  KE3 thyratron tube was replaced during the shutdown, so we wanted to condition the thyratron tube.  During the conditioning of the tube, we would notice KE4 would flatline, so we back downed the voltage to condition at a value where KE4 was stable.  We continued this method and eventually reached the setpoint value.  We then decided to run the system at setpoint for approximately 20 minutes without issues.  We also timed all four traces.  Currently values of the Filament and Reservoir power supplies.  The Booster Extraction Kicker is operating with all four traces.

author: operator_2
subject: SR12 HTS Leads Interlock dark
details: TL;DR: SR12 Quench Detection Chassis was shorting the 24V that also feeds the HTS Leads Chassis.S1225 24V Distribution Chassis CB6 was blowing its fuse. This feeds the 24V to the SR12 Superbend HTS Leads Temperature Interlock Chassis (24W4343). We found that disconnecting SR12 Superbend Quench Detection Chassis (24W2765) PG2 would prevent the fuse from blowing.The 24V signal inside the Quench chassis is used for its Control Room Reset button. The 24V inside the Quench chassis has a capacitor to ground that failed. This shorted the 24V to ground and is what caused the fuse to blow.After replacing the capacitor, everything turned on and reset fine.

author: operator_1
subject: HiPot Test Results on new SRRF HVDC Cables
details: Late Entry:On September 19th, 2024, -60kVDC HiPot testing was conducted and passed on the two new recently pulled in and terminated/installed Dielectric Sciences 2121 High Voltage DC Cables for the Storage Ring RF (SRRF) system for ALS. These cables involve two 150kV rated cables in parallel of approximately 360 foot runs from the outside HVPad Penthouse High Voltage Power Supply Output Disconnect Switch to the SRRF Disconnect Switch above the SRRF Filter Cabinet inside B6 in the RF Area in the SR Pit. These cables were pulled in during the period of 9/11/24 through 9/17/24 by the excellent but also very challenging/physically demanding work of operator_1 and his electricians team including support from the facilities high voltage electricians as well.The cable pulls (both pulling out the old cables and pulling in the new cables) had to be navigated through three zones as follows:1.) High Voltage Pad Penthouse Disconnect Switch down through a conduit with a few right angles to manhole EMH159 between the HVPad and just outside of B6 (with one pull can at the base on the HVPAD system before going underground).2.) Manhole EMH159 (which included a 270 degree routing bend) to the SR Pit First Pull Can inside B6.3.) SR Pit entry pull can through above ground Conduits/Enclosed Wireways with several right angle bends suspended above ground to the SRRF Disconnect Switch above the SRRF Filter Cabinet in the B6 SR Pit RF Area.The electrician team encounterd different challenges at all the various stages but especially in pulling out the old cables in section 1 where the steel flex jackets had corroded through badly in different locations and the cables were essentially stuck/frozen in the conduits in that first section requiring significant pulling and tugging back and forth to free them. Water apparantly had made its way into that portion of the run causing the corrosion. The system may have been living on borrowed time so it was good the cables were replaced. In the future operator_1 and team have recommended Sealtight conduit for better moisture/weather protection for this type of cable run so we are documenting that in this log for the next team that has to do this. The last time the cables were replaced and pulled in was 2013 per the records of operator_2. We are recommending a Preventitive Maintenance schedule of perhaps every 7 years to replace the cables (especially for this next cycle which still has the metal flex jacket and not the Sealtight).The sheer lengths of the cables required staging the new cables all over the ALS SR Pit floor as well as the Booster tunnel roof in prep of pulling the new ones in to the system. New steel flex jackets were used with the new cables. Great care was taken by the Electricians as they pulled in the new cables (delicate balance of not wanting to damage the cables or exceed the pull strength or bend radius specifications while still having to pull them through those above 3 sections). After the cables were pulled in (with extra service loops left at each end), the team of operator_3, operator_4, operator_5, operator_6 and operator_7 focused on the terminations of the cables at each end (primarily on 9/18/24). Again, great care had to be taken to not damage the cables but still strip off the outer jacket and pull back the ground braid (connecting to corona ground donuts) and connect everything on both ends (HVPad Penthouse and SR Pit Disconnect Switches Corona Ball terminations).On 9/19/24 the team of operator_5, operator_8, operator_7 and operator_6 with consulting support / supervision from operator_4 and operator_9 conducted the HiPot testing using the setups shown in the two attached photos. The SRRF kirk key configurations were placed back in the normal operations configurations with both the HVPAD and SR Pit Disconnect Switches engaged to connect that one high voltage cable inside the filter cabinet connected to the HiPot tester shown in the photo all the way through the two parallel long run cables out to the HVPad and through that disconnect switch into the output of the HVPS rectifier output (the latter which included the combination of an equivalent 30 MOhm shunt resistor and reverse biased rectifier diodes in parallel).The results are tabulated in the attached spreadsheet which also contains a plot of the results (generated by operator_8) and two additional pictures within the spreadsheet with one showing the HiPot tester voltage and current displays at 60kVDC and 4.3mA respectively although actually negative polarity (-60kVDC) to match the negative polarity requirements of the klystron cathode voltages and currents. The other picture in the spreadsheet showed the High Voltage Divider Probe measurement visible on the HVPS PLC screen showing the actual negative polarity full voltage (-60kVDC).The results showed around 100uA to 200uA higher HiPot current at the full voltage of -60kVDC vs. the baseline result with the old cables conducted on 6/15/24. Most of the current is due to the parallel combination of the 30 MOhm resistors and reverse biased diodes at the HVPad end. However, this extra 100 to 200uA of current is likely accounted for with the addition of the connection to the 300 MOhm shunt load High Voltage Divider Probe inside the SRRF filter cabinet. It was connected this time but not in that earlier baseline measurement in June.In addition, at the very highest voltages (from -48kVDC to -60kVDC) the current actually peaked and then plateau'd or slight dropped. This could be do to a limitation of the HiPot tester as that same exact behavior was observed in the old baseline measurement in June with the old cables. So it is not due to anything with the cables. There was no evidence of breakdown or arcing (i.e. the HiPot tester did not trip) so this test passed with the new cables thanks to the excellent work of all the different teams throughout this process over the past little over a week or so.  Submitted by operator_9 on 9/20/2024.

author: operator_3
subject: New Golden PVs
details: This summer we added golden PVs for the power supplies in all accelerating sections and completed the golden PVs for the BPMs by adding the missing Bergoz PVs. Also added Setpoint:Error and Setpoint:ErrorFlag PVs for the power supplies and X/Y Error PVs for the BPMs.All the credit goes to , the new PVs are in the beam SIOC and the EPICS DB files were generated by  in Matlab from MML data.  also has updated the cfinit and setcf matlab scripts to cover all 4 accelerating sections and push all MML Family/Field/Device info to channel finder. The cfinit script will be run at each startup by the controls group during the reboot process. The tolerance values for the power supplies are from matlab and placed in the INPA field of Setpoint:ErrorFlag and the alarm limits of Setpoint:Error.In channel finder these are the new tags for power supplies:SetpointGoldenSetpointErrorSetpointErrorFlagThe golden PVs will automatically be updated when the golden lattice file (production or injection) is restored in Matlab and when hwinit is run. There was one small change to skewquads2 SIOC to remove the existing Setpoint:Golden PVs and instead use the PVs from beam. Thanks ![beam R04.50 diff][skewquads2 R01.27 diff]

subject: Displaying and Archiving of noise :)
details: We do not yet generally set deadbands on PVs to avoid displaying and archiving noise !!!!   this is very wastefull of networking bandwidth, and disk space on the archiver.I propose that we start introducing deadbanks to only display and archive significant changes.As an example ....  I propose we start with one of the most interesting values ..., beam current!!!!   do we really need to display uA changes - ????   I propose to set a deadband of 50uA  ....  any objections?
